items.title: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
items.abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. We ask whether pretrained residual transformations can support additional latent computation without expanding the backbone. To test this possibility, we introduce Continuum-LM, which reuses these transformations as dynamical operators in a continuous-depth language model. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. At 0.6B, it also outperforms an Ouro-style recurrent control under matched parameter and residual-function evaluation budgets. Together, these results support extensible computational depth through parameter reuse, identifying continuous hidden-state evolution as a practical design dimension for scientific language models beyond parameter scaling.

items.title: Effects of AI Role and Speech Message Design on Takeover Requests in Automated Driving
items.abstract: AI agents that provide interpretable messages can support clearer communication between humans and automated systems in situations where drivers need to respond within a few seconds. However, the potential of these capabilities to assist drivers during the takeover process remains unknown. Therefore, this study examined the effects of AI roles, explanation type, and directional semantics in speech-based takeover requests on takeover performance, as measured by decision quality (decision-making time and accuracy), and on subjective ratings. Twenty-four participants took part in a within-subjects SAE Level 3 driving simulator study. Among the three AI roles, Advisor AI was associated with faster decision-making times, and Guardian AI was associated with a lower workload. Co-Pilot AI was associated with the slowest decision-making times, lower accuracy, lower trust than Advisor AI, higher anxiety than Guardian AI, the lowest satisfaction, and the highest workload. The ipsilateral display was associated with shorter decision-making times than the contralateral display. Overall, the findings inform the integration of AI into next-generation automated systems.

items.title: EG-GRPO: Evidence-Guided Step-level Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents
items.abstract: LLM-based search agents demonstrate strong capabilities in long-horizon information seeking and reasoning, typically trained via reinforcement learning. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on trajectory-level outcome rewards, providing limited supervision for complex search and reasoning processes. Although step-level credit assignment offers a promising solution, obtaining reliable and task-grounded supervision for open-ended search remains challenging. In this paper, we propose Evidence-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization (EG-GRPO), a framework that derives step-level supervision from the evidence annotations available in synthetic deep search data. EG-GRPO identifies the first supporting citation for each required evidence claim and uses the newly acquired evidence to construct step-level process rewards. By representing the accumulated evidence as an evolving knowledge state, EG-GRPO further performs state-conditioned relative advantage estimation and combines the resulting step-level signal with the standard trajectory-level outcome advantage. Experiments on five challenging deep search benchmarks show that EG-GRPO generally outperforms standard GRPO and existing reward-enhanced and step-level RL baselines across different model scales. These results demonstrate that task-grounded evidence annotations can provide effective process supervision for credit assignment in deep search RL.

items.title: Electrodermal activity as a physiological marker of stress and experience-related differences in workers performing work at heights: A real-world functional data analysis study of certified and novice firefighters
items.abstract: Falls from heights remain a leading cause of fatal workplace accidents, with psychological stress contributing to human error. Electrodermal activity (EDA) and heart rate (HR) are promising stress markers whose real-world, physically demanding applicability remains underexplored. This study examined whether EDA and HR discriminate stress responses between certified and basically trained firefighters, and how these responses evolve across task phases. Seventeen male firefighters from the Moravian-Silesian Region, Czech Republic, completed an ascent, tower-top stay, and rappel from a 50-meter industrial cooling tower. EDA was recorded at the wrist and lumbar region using Sensetio wearable sensors, and HR via a Polar H10+ chest strap. After visual inspection, SCL was extracted from EDA; SCL and HR were both resampled to 600 samples (200 per phase) and min–max normalized. Functional data analysis using point-wise Mann–Whitney U tests, complemented by a cluster-based permutation test for multiple comparisons, compared SCL and HR between groups. SCL increased in both groups, but novices showed an earlier, steeper rise during the ascent and tower-top phases, forming two significant clusters after permutation correction ( t ≈ 59 –213, p c l u s t e r = 0.026 ; t ≈ 219 –421, p c l u s t e r = 0.017 ) with large effect sizes (median r = 0.71 ), whereas certified firefighters showed marked increases mainly during rappelling, where the difference narrowed and lost significance (median r = 0.46 ). No significant between-group HR differences emerged. Normalized SCL trajectories thus captured experience-related timing differences that HR did not, suggesting EDA warrants further investigation as a complement to safety training and monitoring, rather than as a validated readiness or error-risk-prediction tool at this stage.

items.title: Embodied Empathy in VR: Sustained Pro-Animal Attitudes and Behaviors Induced by Simulating Stray Animal Lives
items.abstract: The growing population of stray animals presents pressing ethical and public concerns. We present an extended iStrayPaws, a Virtual Reality Perspective-Taking (VRPT) system combining first-person animal embodiment, shelter narratives, and a virtual behavioral assessment. In a longitudinal study, 48 university students were randomly assigned to VRPT, matched Desktop Perspective-Taking (DPT), or no-intervention Control conditions. State and trait empathy, animal-welfare attitudes, virtual-task performance, and attention were assessed before, immediately after, and one week after intervention. Significant Group × Time interactions emerged across all outcomes (ηp2=.12–0.21). Both VRPT and DPT improved empathy immediately, while VRPT additionally improved task performance and attention. At follow-up, VRPT retained advantages over Control in empathy, welfare attitudes, and task performance, and exceeded DPT in trait-empathy change and task performance. Greater presence was associated with immediate state empathy. Interviews indicated stronger narrative recall, emotional resonance, and welfare-oriented reflection in VRPT. Findings support immersive perspective-taking for sustained cross-species empathy and animal-welfare education.

items.title: EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF WORKPLACE INTERVENTIONS AND OUTCOMES
items.abstract: The health and wellness of employees is now a focal point for companies aiming to optimize employee performance, build robust organizational performance, and ensure sustainable results. This systematic review aims to explore the connection between staff wellbeing and organisational performance, focusing on interventions in the workplace, implementation and outcomes. The review draws together the findings of literature on various interventions, such as the mental health support programs, flexible working arrangements, employee assistance programs, occupational health and safety interventions, leadership development, work–life balance policies, and employee involvement in organizational decision making. The results show that interventions at work that emphasize the psychological, physical and social wellness of workers can benefit job satisfaction, employee engagement, productivity, organizational commitment and retention. The review also emphasizes the need for ‘positive organisational culture', supportive leadership, ‘manageable workloads' and psychologically safe working environments to enhance the effectiveness of well-being strategies. But factors including lack of financial support, poor managerial support, stigma, uneven implementation, and measuring long-term effects may reduce their impact. Contextual factors, such as organizational size, industry attributes, employment conditions, and workforce diversity also play a role in the link between employee well-being and organizational performance. The review concludes that the wellbeing of employees should not be seen as a standalone human resource responsibility, but as a part of the strategy of the organisation. It suggests implementing workplace interventions that are evidence-based, based on inclusiveness, and continually assessed, balancing employee needs and organizational goals. The learnings from these insights are valuable in helping to build a broader picture of how employee well-being programs can contribute to sustainable performance and help managers, HR, and organizational policy makers better guide their employees.

items.title: Enhancing Liver Cirrhosis Diagnosis Using Machine Learning With Explainable AI and Cross-Validated Hyperparameter Tuning Techniques
items.abstract: Cirrhosis is a form of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD) resulting from sustained liver damage from several causes, including viral infection, autoimmune disorders, cholestatic and metabolic disease Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) or heavy alcohol use. Testing for the presence of Liver Cirrhosis (LC) is one of the most critical diagnostics and prognostic assessments for patients. Detecting liver illness in its early stages is challenging as initial symptoms are often mild and difficult to diagnose. Cirrhosis may not present symptoms until an advanced stage, posing a challenge for identification and diagnosis. The lack of explanations for a complex model’s decision-making process creates clinician distrust by concealing the reasoning behind its choices. This research sought to design and assess a novel and non-invasive proposed model by utilizing the XGBoost classifier with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for diagnosing liver cirrhosis. In this work XAI framework enhances transparency in complex models, offering valuable insights into decision-making, thereby guiding treatment strategies, and improving cirrhosis diagnosis. The experimental results have shown superiority for the proposed method compared with various machine learning models. The proposed method has achieved significantly 91.19% using XGBoost for cirrhosis dataset with K-fold validation(K=10) approach.

items.title: Ethics and Governance in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Lifecycle Engineering Perspective
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Trustworthy Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is often treated as a model property addressed through better training data, alignment, evaluation or guardrails. We argue instead that trustworthiness is a lifecycle governance capability that must be engineered, evidenced, monitored and adapted across data acquisition, training and alignment, safe inference, public deployment and post‐deployment use. We develop a lifecycle engineering framework integrating four governance layers – technical, organizational, human‐centred and regulatory – and translate ethical principles and major governance instruments into stage‐specific controls, responsibilities, evidence artefacts, metrics and review triggers. The framework is constructed through a structured conceptual synthesis of peer‐reviewed literature, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, ISO/IEC 42005, ALTAI, the EU AI Act and complementary security and agentic‐governance guidance. A source register, seven‐field extraction schema, explicit mapping rules, worked extraction example and weighting sensitivity analysis make the construction logic inspectable. items.title: Evaluating the Biomechanical and Ergonomic Effects of Framing Nail Guns Among Residential Carpenters: A Within-Subject Comparison of Three Commonly Used Tools
items.abstract: Nail guns are essential for residential framing, yet comparative evidence on how different tools influence physical workload and vibration exposure remains limited. This study evaluated the biomechanical and ergonomic implications of three framing nail guns commonly used in Australian residential construction. Nineteen carpenters completed a controlled laboratory protocol informed by field-based task analysis. Wearable sensors and motion capture quantified biomechanical and exposure differences among tool conditions. Measures included body movement, muscle activity, operating forces, vibration exposure, upper-limb demand, and overall workload. Compared with Tool A, Tool B and Tool C produced higher shoulder and wrist loading; higher relative sEMG RMS amplitude, reaching up to 161% of the Tool A reference value; and increased vibration exposure of 4.57 m/s2 and 4.98 m/s2, respectively, compared with 3.89 m/s2 for Tool A. They also showed lower comfort and balance ratings (p<0.001). These findings demonstrate distinct exposure profiles among the evaluated tool conditions; however, the fixed testing order and the absence of experimental manipulation of individual design characteristics preclude attribution of the observed differences to specific tool-design features.

items.title: Evidence-Grounded LLM-Assisted Android Mobile Forensic Reporting
items.abstract: Large language models can assist forensic report drafting, but fluent output does not ensure evidentiary reliability. This study presents an evidence-grounded framework for evaluating LLM-assisted Android forensic reports at the atomic-claim level. Gemini, Llama, and Qwen each generated reports for two controlled cases: a public Android 13 dataset and a physical LG device with a zero-reportable-fact boundary. The six accepted reports were decomposed into 612 claims and evaluated against frozen, human-reviewed authorities through content labeling, citation validation, fact-recall analysis, independent rechecking, and dispute resolution. The final corpus contained 424 supported, 163 unsupported, four contradicted, four overstated or incomplete, and 17 excluded claims. In the public case, all three models recovered all 27 authorized report-level facts. Citation validity nevertheless differed substantially: Gemini produced 168 valid citations from 189 required citations, Qwen produced 145 from 189, and Llama produced none from 135. In the physical device case, the models generated 65 claims despite the zero reportable-fact boundary, including 38 unsupported and one contradicted claim. These results show that evidence restriction and complete fact recall do not guarantee claim support or valid evidence attribution. The framework provides an auditable method for detecting unsupported content, preserving claim-to evidence lineage, and retaining investigator authority over final forensic reports.

items.title: Evidence-State Drift: A Claim-Level Framework and Replay Benchmark for Web-Connected LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Evidence-State Drift, a claim-level framework for monitoring changes in evidence used by web-connected large language model (LLM) agents over repeated retrieval events. The framework represents evidence using a normalized claim, evidence span, source identity, retrieval and publication timestamps, content fingerprint, and source-authority label. It aims to distinguish material changes in claim-associated evidence from non-material modifications, such as formatting changes, that do not alter the monitored claim. The study evaluates the proposed representation using a longitudinal replay benchmark containing 67 claims and 871 observation events, including 47 oracle-defined material changes. Within this benchmark, the claim-state detector achieved an F1 score of 0.989 against a predefined deterministic change oracle, with no false positives among 824 oracle-defined non-material events. These results indicate consistency with the benchmark’s predefined change rules. They do not establish independent semantic validation or improved factual accuracy in deployed LLM agents. Independent human evaluation and end-to-end agent testing remain areas for future work. This research contributes to the study of evidence monitoring, information freshness, data provenance, and reliability in web-connected AI systems.

items.title: Examining the Possible Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Institutions: A Preliminary Investigation into Management Colleges in Jaipur
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has established itself as an engine for change in a variety of disciplines, reinventing operations, making decisions, and processes. AI has incredible potential in education that could enhance educational experiences, optimise administrative processes, and promote personalised education (Sadiku, M. N. et al, 2022). As educational institutions attempt to meet the needs of the digital age, investigating AI applications becomes critical (Pedro, F., et al., 2019). This early inquiry intends to look into the potential uses of AI in management colleges in Jaipur, India. The incorporation of AI into educational institutions has the potential to overcome a number of difficulties that exist in the traditional educational framework. As stated by Rane, N. et al. (2023), AI-powered technology can provide personalised learning experiences tailored to specific student needs, increasing student engagement and boosting learning results. Furthermore, AI-driven analytics can provide useful insights into studentperformance trends, allowing for early intervention measures to address academic issues (Jones et al., 2019). The landscape of AI use in educational institutions is rapidly changing. AI-powered chatbots are being used by institutions around the world to handle administrative activities like admissions, course registrations, and student inquiries (Alvarez, 2018). Furthermore, AI-powered learning management systems (LMS) are being used to provide adaptive learning experiences that dynamically modify content delivery based on student success and personal preferences (Wang et al., 2021)

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Management Information Systems: From Prediction to Managerial Decision-Making
items.abstract: The use of machine-learning models in management information systems enables organizations to generate predictions at increasing scale and speed. Predictive performance alone, however, is insufficient for managerial use. Decision makers also need to examine why an output was produced, interpret the explanation within the decision context, and monitor the consequences of resulting actions. This chapter treats explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) as an intermediate layer between machine-learning predictions and managerial decision-making. It integrates the literatures on decision support systems, human collaboration with artificial intelligence (AI), and human-centered XAI evaluation. To maintain a focused technical scope, the chapter examines two widely used methods for explaining the outputs of trained models: Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Drawing on the literature reviewed, the chapter develops a four-layer framework that connects prediction, explanation, managerial interpretation and evaluation, and decision, action, and feedback. Published studies from manufacturing, finance and credit, and energy management are then used to examine how these four layers appear in different application settings. The analysis indicates that explanations do not automatically produce trust, decision quality, or ethical acceptability. Their managerial value depends on the joint evaluation of technical properties, user and task characteristics, organizational context, and governance arrangements.

items.title: Explainable temporal deep learning for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using IoT sensor data
items.abstract: Concrete compressive strength is a fundamental indicator of structural performance, yet conventional destructive testing methods require 7–28 days, limiting timely decision-making in construction projects. This study presents an interpretable deep learning framework for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using real-time multivariate Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The proposed approach integrates internal curing conditions (temperature and humidity), ambient environmental variables, and mix design parameters to model early-age hydration dynamics as a temporal learning problem. A Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network with an attention mechanism is developed to capture both forward and backward temporal dependencies in the curing process while identifying the most influential time intervals. To ensure interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and attention-based analysis are incorporated to quantify feature importance and reveal critical curing stages governing strength development. The model is trained and validated using field data collected from real construction sites, enabling evaluation under realistic environmental variability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high predictive accuracy (MAE = 1.52 MPa, R 2 = 0.94), outperforming benchmark models including GRU, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), and conventional machine learning approaches. Unlike existing studies that primarily rely on laboratory-controlled datasets or focus on prediction without early-stage applicability, the proposed framework enables reliable estimation of 7-day and 28-day compressive strength within the first 24–48 h of curing. This combination of real-time IoT sensing, temporal deep learning, and explainable artificial intelligence provides a robust and practical decision-support tool for smart construction systems, enabling improved quality control, optimized scheduling, and reduced reliance on destructive testing.

items.title: Explaining cyberbullying and cyber violence in the age of AI using individual and contextual factors in Jordan
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies continue to transform online communication and social interactions, cyberbullying and cyber-violence have emerged as growing concerns that require a deeper understanding of the individual and contextual factors underlying these behaviors. This study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing cyberbullying and cyber-violence in Jordan. Specifically, it examines the effects of individual characteristics and contextual factors, including the legal and policy environment and aggressive social environment, on both cyberbullying and cyber-violence. A total of 472 participants from different demographic groups were included in the study sample. The data were analyzed using Smart PLS software. The results indicate that individual factors such as age, gender, and educational level have varying effects on cyberbullying and cyber-violence. Both age and gender have a significant negative and positive relationship, respectively, with both cyberbullying and cyber-violence. There is no significant relationship between these outcomes and educational level. Contextual factors, on the other hand, have differential effects. The aggressive social environment is positively associated with cyberbullying and cyber-violence, while the legal and policy environment is negatively associated with cyber-violence but not with cyberbullying. This study examines both contextual and individual factors, contributing to a better understanding of factors influencing cyberbullying and cyber-violence. It provides evidence on the impact of age, gender, social context, and legal and regulatory influences, and offers insights that can guide policy, education, and community engagement and inform best prevention practices.

items.title: Explicit Discontinuance and Switching Signals in Generative AI Applications: A Comparative Analysis across Nine Apps
items.abstract: This study examines explicitly reported discontinuance and platform-switching signals in Turkish- and English-language Google Play reviews of nine generative artificial intelligence applications. A total of 1,145,267 reviews posted between 1 July 2025 and 30 June 2026 were screened using rule-based procedures. Of 11,960 candidate reviews, 821 that met strict contextual rules were evaluated in two blind AI-assisted coding passes. The final high-confidence analysis set comprised 692 records, including 543 signals in which discontinuance or switching was reported as having occurred and 149 signals expressing discontinuance intention. To assess the recall limitation of the strict screen, an additional application-by-language stratified sample of 500 reviews was audited from the broader pool of 11,139 records, revealing 110 missed explicit signals. The stratified weighted estimate of the proportion of missed explicit signals in the broad pool was 21.6% (95% CI: 18.2%-25.2%). Accordingly, rates reported per 10,000 reviews are interpreted as high-confidence detection indicators rather than prevalence estimates. Within the high-confidence set, the most frequent reasons were response quality/task failure, technical problems, privacy/trust, and pricing. Among platform switches reported as having occurred, Gemini and Claude were the most frequent destinations. By separating intention from signals of reported enacted behavior and by explicitly reporting screening sensitivity, this study provides complementary evidence to the post-adoption literature on generative AI.

items.title: Explore or Confirm? LLM Agents Misallocate Measurements Under Noise
items.abstract: As model reasoning gets cheaper, the physical experiment becomes the slow and costly step in discovery. Each experiment returns a noisy reading: a high value can mean a good candidate or a lucky draw. With a fixed budget, an AI agent must keep choosing between exploring a new candidate and confirming a promising one by re-testing it. We measure that choice in Wellocate, a simulated assay campaign with known true values. It is built on a generated landscape and on two real protein datasets, GB1 and PhoQ, scrambled so no model can answer from memory. We test five language models as minimal agents, with no tools and no memory beyond the history in each prompt. They misallocate in both directions. Three over-confirm, spending most of the budget re-testing. On the generated landscape one under-confirms, trusting single readings, and there every model ends with a worse final pick than a basic scripted strategy. Each failure has its own cause. The over-confirmers run short of new candidates worth trying: a list of untried candidates cuts their re-testing and, on real protein data, makes two of them pick much better. A running summary of their readings or a description of the landscape changes it by at most five percentage points. For the under-confirmer, re-testing its top candidates in a final round, replayed on its own campaigns, recovers only about a quarter of what it loses by picking the wrong candidate. This suggests confirmation has to run through the whole campaign. We release Wellocate as a benchmark and reinforcement-learning environment with frozen splits and scripted baselines. With it, anyone can measure how an agent splits its budget before trusting it with real experiments, and train agents to split it better. Code, data and the environment are available at https://github.com/Xstendyl/wellocate.

items.title: Fostering self-management competencies through AI-based coaching: mechanisms of inhibition and approach motivation, and intrinsic goal motivation
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based coaching helps individuals attain their goals, yet its effects on self-management and the mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. Self-management includes self-regulation, self-access, self-control, and volitional facilitation. We hypothesised that the anonymous and nonjudgmental nature of AI-based coaching reduces inhibition and fosters approach motivation, activating intrinsic goal motivation and supporting self-management processes. In a quasi-experimental controlled trial (N = 111), we compared an AI-based coach (chatbot) with a self-coaching intervention (control condition). No significant Condition × Time interactions were observed for the outcome variables. Exploratory pairwise comparisons indicated improvements in self-regulation in both conditions. Within-group patterns suggested increased volitional facilitation following AI-based coaching and increased self-access following self-coaching. No significant effects emerged for self-control. Path analyses revealed that during coaching, chatbot users felt less inhibited and more approach-motivated than self-coaching users, which boosted their motivation to work on their goals and strengthened self-management. The findings suggest that AI-based coaching may foster self-management and that these effects may emerge through motivational processes. Whether the relationship plays a less central role in AI-based coaching than in human coaching remains an open question.

items.title: From Ancient Records to Agentic Intelligence: A Comprehensive Historical Review of Data Science and Its Role in Intelligent Internet of Things Analytics
items.abstract: Since the era of the Mesopotamia between 2900 BCE - 2350 BCE, the goals of “data science-like” approaches have always revolved around collecting fragments of information and trying to make insights out of such information. Data Science was not clearly termed as Data Science from the onset. Moreover, there exists several questions about Data Science just been a polished name for Statistics. Therefore, there is a need to look carefully at how Data Science has evolved over the years and where it is currently. The study defines Data Science as a multidisciplinary field that integrates statistics, mathematics, computer science, domain expertise, and ethics. This is important because, it will give Data Scientists and the Data Science enthusiasts a clear understanding of this discipline. In addition, the paper demonstrates how Data Science transforms massive Internet of Things (IoT) data streams into actionable insights through predictive analytics, anomaly detection, explainable artificial intelligence, cybersecurity analytics, digital twins, and intelligent decision support. The findings reveal that the evolution of Data Science reflects a transition from descriptive statistical analysis to autonomous, explainable, and trustworthy intelligent systems capable of supporting real-time decision-making across diverse domains. This work provides a unified historical perspective, highlights emerging research directions, and offers a valuable reference for researchers, educators, and practitioners seeking to understand the past, present, and future direction of Data Science.

items.title: From Concept to Production
items.abstract: This article examines the potential integration of artificial intelligence tools into the filmmaking process, with a focus on the Pre-Production stage, which includes the design, development, and preparation of production, especially for animated films. Through interviews with experts, literature review, open-source tool testing, and participation in real film projects, the study examines the creative and technical roles that AI can assume during Pre‑Production. The research analyzes how AI technologies influence early production workflows and evaluates their broader impact on the production pipeline through comparative assessments and real‑world applications. Adopting a dual methodological approach that combines a systematic literature review with an applied experimental study, the article moves from a conceptual examination of AI’s capabilities to a collaborative, practice‑based experimental investigation.The first experiment provides a comprehensive review of available AI tools, while the second presents a practical experiment in which students and industry professionals collaborated to create short films using AI‑driven production methods. The study aims to highlight the possibilities, limitations, and challenges arising from AI integration in the pre-production of animated films, contributing to the discussion on the evolution of the film industry and the use of modern technologies in the creative process.

items.title: From Coursework to Digital Da’wah Practice: Knowledge Application and Motivation among Islamic Religious Education Students
items.abstract: Purpose of the study: This study examines how Islamic Religious Education students apply knowledge acquired through da’wah coursework in social media practices, adapt communication methods, and describe their motivations for producing and sharing religious content. Method: A qualitative case study involved nine purposively selected participants: six students engaged in digital da’wah, one course lecturer, and two audience members. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, nonparticipant observation, and documentation. Analysis followed Miles and Huberman’s model of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Credibility was addressed through source and methodological triangulation. Main findings: Knowledge application involved planning, production, distribution, and unevenly articulated evaluation across Instagram, TikTok, and WhatsApp. Students reported selecting religious sources, adapting messages to audiences, and using varied visual and written formats. Advice-oriented communication was prominent, while audience adaptation and reported question-and-answer exchanges reflected aspects of bil hikmah and mujadalah. Some students revised presentation following feedback, whereas others reported limited audience criticism. Participation combined creative enjoyment, religious commitments, coursework experiences, social encouragement, and audience responses. These motivations overlapped rather than following a uniform developmental sequence. Engagement metrics did not establish audience understanding or behavioural change. Novelty/Originality of this study: The study integrates knowledge application, da’wah methods, and motivation within one educational case, interpreting digital da’wah as situated practice rather than assuming that coursework completion or frequent posting demonstrates comprehensive competence. Contributions of this study: The findings inform practical course design that combines content production with source verification, audience-sensitive communication, responsible dialogue, and structured reflection. They also distinguish religious commitment from intrinsic motivation and identify feedback use as an important dimension requiring further pedagogical attention in religious education.

items.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
items.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.

items.title: From Label Priors to Task Evidence: Efficient Long-Video Frame Selection via Bayesian GRPO
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Existing retrieval-based approaches typically rely on supervised learning from static keyframe annotations. However, these label priors often fail to align with the actual information required by downstream MLLMs for complex reasoning, creating a misalignment between the training target and inference needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a probabilistic framework that reformulates frame selection as latent-variable inference. We first initialize a lightweight policy using supervised learning to capture general visual saliency. Then, we treat a frozen MLLM as a task environment and use its answer likelihood as dense task evidence to refine the policy via Bayesian Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Within this formulation, the negative log-likelihood (NLL) over ground-truth answer tokens provides a principled dense reward, while a prior-matching KL term preserves semantic consistency with the elicited label prior. This process transitions the selection principle from static label priors to task evidence. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that our selector achieves competitive accuracy with MLLM-based scorers while retaining the inference efficiency of lightweight methods. The selector is trained once with a frozen MLLM environment and transfers directly to multiple downstream MLLMs without retraining. Code is available at \url{github.com/Miraclecsc/Frame_Selection_GRPO}.

items.title: From MSCA Proposal to the Ubuntu-Duende Lab: Embodiment, Digital Pedagogy, and the Intrinsic Pace of the Body
items.abstract: In this paper, I articulate the transition from my 2025 Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal into an independent, sovereign research lab. The MSCA proposal entitled DUENDE: Decolonial Ubuntu Embodiment for New Dance Epistemologies, was conceptualised as an exploratory research design for a two-year Practice-as-Research (PaR) study at the University of Granada. Its purpose was to propose and test an accessible digital pedagogy for the transcultural transmission of Flamenco in resource-constrained environments. I explain how centering embodiment as my primary epistemology exposed a fundamental tension between institutional grant timelines and the physical limits of the human body. In an era dominated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and hyper-accelerated "Fast Science," somatic integration, habitus, and tissue memory operate on an un-hurried, non-linear tempo. By depositing a summaries of the MSCA proposal methodology, workplan, and flow diagram on on Zenodo as an open-access research blueprint, I pivot away from administrative grant structures to launch the Ubuntu Duende Lab (fea-udl). Grounded in daily living practice, Substack peer-review (@kitaraflamenca), and low-bandwidth digital tools subverted for sovereign pedagogy, this paper establishes an autonomous research framework designed to unfold at the intrinsic speed of the body.

items.title: From Proposal to Execution: Modeling Interaction Semantics in Shared Autonomy
items.abstract: In many human-AI systems, candidate actions are not executed directly but are first evaluated by another decision-making entity under a potentially different objective or decision model. Standard decision-theoretic frameworks do not require this interaction to be represented explicitly, as they define transition dynamics directly over state-action pairs, allowing evaluation to be absorbed within the transition model. We introduce a semantics-aware decision framework in which a candidate action is proposed, evaluated under an interaction context, and then resolved into an executed outcome. We formalize this through a joint action language and an interpretation function that maps each joint action and context to a semantic outcome. Transition and reward dynamics are induced through these semantic outcomes, thereby introducing an explicit representational layer for interaction semantics. Semantic outcomes provide explicit units for organizing interaction principles, which can be instantiated through application-specific evaluation mechanisms and reused across distinct interaction instances. This provides a structured interface for specifying context-dependent evaluation separately from the resulting execution dynamics, without requiring changes to the underlying planning algorithm. We instantiate the framework in shared human-AI autonomy, capturing interaction patterns such as advisory and authorization, and illustrating how interaction context influences decision making. The resulting formulation remains compatible with standard Markov decision process (MDP) planning.

items.title: From the Wiki Incident through Car and Property Metaphors to a Topology of an AI Civilization
items.abstract: Version 1.00 This essay develops a conceptual framework for the emerging infrastructure of an AI civilization, starting from a concrete real-world incident involving AI agents acting on public wikis. Using the metaphors of a traffic accident and of agents entering another party’s digital property, it derives step by step a set of practical requirements: agent identification, a responsibility address, run or session identity, respect for local rules, incident reconstruction, liability, insurance, certification, and shared responsibility across operators, platforms, model providers, and other actors. The essay does not propose a complete regulatory system. Its method is deliberately incremental: introduce only what becomes necessary from the next concrete problem, and allow institutions and standards to evolve from practice. An accompanying appendix maps these ideas to parallel work already under way in research, standardisation, regulation, and industry, including agent identity, delegation, auditability, incident reporting, insurance, certification, and machine-readable website policies. The central proposal is not a new theory of AI governance, but a way of seeing how already emerging pieces may fit into a broader topology of relationships among actors, spaces, permissions, actions, damage, responsibility, and institutions.

items.title: From Unverifiable Domain Text to Cross-Lingual RLVR via Code-Switched Task Synthesis
items.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) can improve reasoning in large language models, but specialized non-English domains expose a data mismatch. Raw English domain text is often available, while target-language RLVR tasks with verifiable rewards are scarce. We introduce code-switched task synthesis for cross-lingual RLVR, a data-centric approach that derives target-language and code-switched RLVR task variants from otherwise unverifiable English domain text. Using fill-in-the-middle multiple-choice QA as a seed task format, we synthesize automatically verifiable tasks from domain passages and reshape them into cross-lingual variants. These variants preserve the same evidence-answer relation but change how English and target-language evidence are presented during RLVR. On Korean medical benchmarks and cybersecurity benchmarks across four target languages, code-switched training outperforms matched monolingual and bilingual-mixture baselines on average target-language performance while maintaining comparable English performance. Additional analyses provide evidence of better target-language input understanding and stronger cross-lingual alignment in both model outputs and internal representations. These results suggest that code-switched training helps target-language inputs access domain reasoning learned more strongly in English.

items.title: FTFM: Factorized Tabular Foundation Models
items.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are becoming a powerful alternative to conventional tabular learning, adapting to new datasets in context without task-specific training. Current architectures, however, face a trade-off: models that preserve cell-level representations are expensive because they repeatedly attend across rows and columns, while faster models collapse each row into a fixed embedding and lose this fine-grained state. We introduce Factorized Tabular Foundation Models (FTFM), which preserve cell representations while factorizing their computation through one contextual latent per row and one per column. Cells no longer attend to one another directly; instead, each cell is updated through the interaction of its row and column latents, reducing repeated attention while retaining feature-specific information. FTFM achieves competitive predictive performance in tabular classification on major benchmarks such as TabArena and BeyondArena.

items.title: Generative AI Engine for Energy Materials Intelligence and Manufacturing
items.abstract: Energy materials development remains experimentally intensive because relevant knowledge is dispersed across heterogeneous sources, material formulas and processing parameters are strongly coupled, and experimental data are often incomplete. Although artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), can support knowledge extraction, materials design, experiment planning and data analysis, these capabilities often operate as isolated tools rather than as a computational–experimental loop. This Perspective proposes a conceptual 4E framework—comprising Extraction, Execution, Evolution, and a Generative AI (GAI) Engine—for energy Materials Intelligence and Manufacturing. Extraction converts literature, experimental records, and multimodal data into structured knowledge. Execution translates encoded recipes into machine-executable protocols for robotic synthesis and characterization while returning real-time feedback. Evolution uses robotic experimental feedback to evaluate a domain-specific Recipe Language Model (RLM), which subsequently recommends new material recipes. The GAI Engine coordinates the RLM, materials database, robotic platform, characterization systems, and digital twin within a closed-loop architecture. The framework is further extended conceptually towards intelligent manufacturing through operational data, process monitoring, quality control, and staged translation from laboratory validation to pilot and industrial operation. The 4E framework therefore provides a pathway, grounded in experimentally demonstrated platforms, that links knowledge, formulas and parameters, robotic execution and feedback-driven learning for Materials Intelligence and Manufacturing.

items.title: Generative AI in Higher Education: Global Trends, Challenges, and Policy Implications
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral tool to a routine feature of student life in higher education.This paper examines how generative AI, and ChatGPT specifically, is used across global and regional student populations, and what challenges accompany that use.Drawing on secondary analysis of four public survey datasets, including a global sample of 23,218 students across 110 countries (Ravšelj et al., 2025) and three available regional datasets from Bangladesh, Colombia, and Ecuador, the study addresses three research questions concerning prevalence and institutional readiness, task level application and regional variation, and the ethical and institutional challenges tied to AI adoption.Results show that 71.4% of the global sample had used ChatGPT, primarily for brainstorming, summarizing, and research assistance, though usage intensity and institutional policy awareness varied meaningfully by region.The three regional datasets converge on a common theme even though each measure it differently: a substantial share of students report reduced verification behavior and self-perceived overreliance on AI tools, a pattern this paper terms experienced dependency to distinguish it from the abstract ethical concern measured by the global dataset.The paper argues that adoption, ethical concern, and experienced dependency function as related but distinct dimensions rather than opposite poles of a single spectrum, and that institutions should track them independently.Implications for policy, faculty development, and future research are discussed.

items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has moved within a few years from experimental tool to routine instrument in marketing departments, and the academic literature is still catching up with that speed. This chapter offers a structured review of work published between 2020 and 2026 on how GenAI is used in marketing, how consumers respond to it, and which governance questions follow. Drawing on journal articles from marketing, information systems, economics and law, together with regulatory documents from the European Union and Türkiye, the chapter first separates predictive from generative systems and maps their uses in content production, personalization, customer interaction and marketing research. It then organizes the consumer evidence around three recurring themes: task-dependent preference for machine advice, authenticity penalties attached to perceived AI authorship, and the ambiguous effects of humanlike design in service encounters. Field and experimental studies of workplace use point to productivity gains that are uneven across workers, while creativity research shows a tension between individual output quality and collective diversity. The chapter also discusses hallucination, representational bias, privacy and dark patterns, the energy demand of large models, and the transparency duties introduced by the EU Artificial Intelligence Act alongside Turkish data protection guidance. Much of the evidence rests on short online experiments and on firms in North America and Europe, so conclusions about long-term behavior and about Türkiye remain provisional. The chapter closes with a research agenda on longitudinal field designs, disclosure formats, cross-cultural replication and the measurement of environmental cost in marketing operations. For managers, the evidence suggests that the source, tone and disclosure of generated content matter as much as its quality.

items.title: Gig Workers and Platform Labour: Social Security, Employee Status, and the Legal Fight Over Classification
items.abstract: Digital labour platforms have revolutionised the nature of work by allowing people to offer transportation, delivery, domestic and professional services through technology-based intermediaries. While platform-based work is flexible and provides opportunities for income generation, it also poses serious legal issues relating to the classification of work, social security, fair compensation, occupational safety and the allocation of responsibility among the worker, the platform and the State. The central problem is that platforms often label workers as independent contractors while exercising significant control over the workers’ access to work, pricing, performance measurement and continued participation through algorithmic systems. This leaves a gap between the formal categorisation of workers and the economic nature of the working relationship. This paper explores the connection between worker classification and social security, focusing on the changing landscape of labour law in India. It examines the Code on Social Security, 2020, which recognises gig workers and platform workers, and assesses the extent to which the statutory framework is sufficient to address their vulnerability. It also considers the constitutional concepts of equality, dignity and social justice, the judicial history of employment classification, and international approaches such as those of the United Kingdom and the United States. The study is doctrinal and comparative, drawing on legislation, judicial decisions, government reports, international standards and academic literature. The paper concludes that the recognition of gig and platform workers as separate statutory categories is a significant step, but not sufficient to ensure effective social protection or to resolve the question of employment status. A classification system that is largely contractual and based on labels may allow platforms to evade responsibility for what they actually control. The paper therefore proposes a functional, multi-factor classification test, portable social security benefits, transparent algorithmic management, fair contribution-sharing and accessible dispute-resolution mechanisms. It concludes that India needs a worker-centred regulatory regime that allows for genuine flexibility without shifting undue economic risk onto workers.

items.title: gKSM: GPU Memory Deduplication at Driver Layer for Serverless LLM Inference
items.abstract: In serverless LLM inference, cloud providers commonly locate multiple instances on a single GPU to improve utilization. However, each instance independently maintains its model weights and runtime state, making duplicate GPU memory the primary bottleneck. Memory deduplication is a widely-used technique for eliminating duplicate data in CPU systems, but extending it to GPU memory faces fundamental challenges. Effective GPU memory deduplication must avoid redundant data movement between CPU and GPU while preserving write isolation for shared pages without native copy-on-write (COW) support. This paper presents gKSM, a transparent GPU memory deduplication framework for serverless LLM inference. gKSM addresses these challenges through CPU-GPU collaborative hash management that offloads hash computation to GPU kernels, zero-copy model weight deduplication that eliminates duplication before model weight transfer, and a cross-privilege page fault handler that combines a lightweight kernel hook and CUDA Virtual Memory Management (VMM) remapping in the user space. gKSM also designs a stable page scanning algorithm and a reuse-aware placement policy in cluster scale. Experiments show that gKSM reduces GPU memory usage by 59.8% while maintaining high throughput compared to ServerlessLLM. Under memory constrained workloads, gKSM improves aggregate throughput by 2.15X and supports five instances concurrently. In cluster level simulation, gKSM achieves a service rate of 99.97%, compared to 78.2% for SLInfer and 26.9% for ServerlessLLM.

items.title: Global Research Trends in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Drug Delivery Technology: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis (2015–2026)
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as transformative technologies in pharmaceutical research, significantly influencing the design, optimization, and personalization of drug delivery systems.AI-assisted approaches are increasingly applied to predict drug release kinetics, optimize formulation parameters, identify novel drug carriers, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and accelerate pharmaceutical product development.Despite the rapid growth of this interdisciplinary research area, a comprehensive understanding of its global scientific evolution, collaborative networks, and emerging research themes remains limited.The present study aims to systematically map the global research landscape of AI and ML applications in drug delivery technology through a bibliometric analysis of publications published between 2015 and 2026.Bibliographic records will be retrieved from the Scopus database using a predefined search strategy, screened according to established inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using Bibliometrix (R-package) and VOSviewer.The study will evaluate annual publication trends, citation performance, influential authors, institutions, countries, journals, collaborative networks, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and emerging research hotspots.The findings are expected to provide a comprehensive overview of the intellectual structure and development of AI-driven drug delivery research, identify influential contributors and collaborative patterns, and highlight promising directions for future investigations.The study also seeks to offer practical insights for researchers, pharmaceutical scientists, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and industry stakeholders by identifying technological innovations that can enhance drug development processes and improve patient-centric therapeutic outcomes.By integrating bibliometric techniques with science mapping, this study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-enabled pharmaceutical technologies and provides a strategic research agenda for advancing intelligent drug delivery systems.

items.title: Governance of AI-Enabled Digital Health Systems: Integrating Clinical Safety, Cybersecurity, Interoperability and Regulatory Compliance in the NHS
items.abstract: Digital health technologies, including mobile applications, clinical decision-support systems, software-based medical technologies and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools, are increasingly integrated into healthcare delivery. Within the UK National Health Service (NHS), these technologies offer opportunities to improve patient outcomes, operational efficiency and data-driven clinical decision-making. Their implementation, however, introduces complex challenges relating to medical device qualification and classification, clinical safety, cybersecurity, interoperability, data governance and regulatory compliance.This study examines the regulatory and governance frameworks applicable to AI-enabled digital health and medical device systems within the NHS, with particular emphasis on the Clinical Risk Management Standards DCB0129 and DCB0160, the Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC), and relevant UK medical device regulatory requirements. A structured literature review was conducted using PubMed, covering publications between 2015 and 2025. Sixty studies were included and analysed using a narrative synthesis approach to identify recurring regulatory, technical and governance challenges associated with the implementation and lifecycle management of digital health technologies.The findings indicate that existing NHS frameworks provide an important foundation for clinical safety, data protection, cybersecurity and organisational assurance. However, their application becomes increasingly complex for interconnected and adaptive AI-enabled systems. Key challenges include uncertainty in medical device qualification and regulatory classification, fragmentation across governance requirements, algorithmic bias and explainability, data integrity, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, interoperability, limitations in conventional evaluation approaches, and the need for continuous monitoring of system performance following implementation.Drawing on these findings, this study proposes a Unified NHS AI Governance and Compliance Model that integrates medical device qualification and regulatory classification with clinical safety, data protection, cybersecurity, usability and accessibility, interoperability, and data and AI workflow governance. The model provides a structured lifecycle approach to support early determination of regulatory requirements, clearer allocation of organisational responsibilities, proportionate risk assessment, implementation assurance and post-deployment monitoring.The study concludes that governance of AI-enabled digital health and medical device technologies should evolve towards a more integrated, adaptive and risk-based approach that aligns medical device regulation with wider digital-health assurance requirements. Although developed within the NHS context, the proposed framework may provide a transferable governance approach for healthcare organisations implementing complex, interoperable and AI-enabled digital technologies.

items.title: Harm Spot Detection using Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
items.abstract: Crime is a major concern in urban and semi-urban areas, and identifying locations where crime risk may be higher can support better planning and resource allocation. This project presents an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning based Crime Hotspots Detection system that uses location-based crime-related features to estimate the risk level of a selected geographical point. The system combines a web-based map interface with a machine learning backend. A user selects a location on an interactive map, the frontend sends latitude and longitude to the backend API, and the backend extracts relevant features and applies a trained XGBoost model to predict the crime-risk category. The result is returned to the user as a risk score and a category such as Low, Medium, or High. The system is designed to provide an easy-to-understand visual representation of potential crime-risk areas and can support data-driven analysis and planning.

items.title: HEALTHCARE AI
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in healthcare to support access to information, patient engagement, administrativeefficiency, and selected clinical workflows. This paper proposes a Healthcare AI framework that organizes healthcare-related requests andprovides structured, understandable information through a digital interface. The framework combines a user interface, request classification,retrieval from approved healthcare information sources, privacy and safety checks, and a response-generation layer. It can support generalhealth education, service navigation, and appointment-related guidance where authorized services are available. The system is designed tocommunicate uncertainty, protect sensitive information, and direct users to qualified professionals when a request is outside its scope. It is notintended to diagnose conditions, prescribe treatment, or replace clinical judgement. The proposed design is modular and can be evaluatedthrough documented software, usability, source-quality, privacy, and safety tests

items.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning
items.abstract: Given the high cost of expert annotation and limited fine-tuning resources, effective data selection from large unlabeled pools under strict budgets has become a crucial step in adapting LLMs to specialized domains. Existing label-dependent methods risk distorted selection when using pseudo-labels, while traditional active learning methods do not explicitly characterize instruction-tuning dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose Hidden Cartographer (HC), a two-stage framework that uses hidden states to guide annotation and exact training dynamics to select the final training subset. The first stage is Progressive Candidate Expansion, which utilizes the proxy to iteratively select top unlabeled candidates for expert annotation, merging them to recompute training dynamics and update the proxy until the annotation budget is exhausted; the second stage is Exact Cartography Pruning, which ranks these annotated candidates by their exact dynamics scores to isolate a compact subset under the final training budget. Experiments across the medical, legal, and financial domains demonstrate that HC achieves the highest average accuracy among all budgeted baselines, requiring annotation for only 20--30% of the original pool and fine-tuning on just 10--15%.

items.title: How AI developers acquire training data: six channels and the shift away from the open web
items.abstract: Developers of large AI models obtain training data through six channels: collection from the open web without a licence, licences from publishers and platforms, commissioned human and expert work, the purchase or licence of organisations' internal records, purpose-built environments and synthetic data, and data from their own users and devices. This paper describes each channel from a public-record compilation read on 18 October 2026: 122 quantified supply facts, 111 disclosed licensing deals, 83 lawsuits, rulings and regulatory actions, 227 financial records of data vendors, 111 funding events, 110 brokerage records and 1,022 price observations, with a robots.txt census of 6,094 websites. The open web remains the largest source by volume, but access is narrowing: 11.4 percent of the census sites shut at least one AI crawler out of the whole site, and an earlier audit found restrictions on 28 percent or more of the most actively maintained sources of a standard web corpus. Of the 83 legal records, 70 concern content taken without a licence and 12 concern developers' use of their own users' data; none concerns the channels in which developers pay for data. Money is moving to those paid channels: disclosed licences, data vendors whose newest reported revenues or run rates exceed one billion dollars, and, since 2026, published programmes that buy organisations' records. We set out the scale, prices and legal exposure of each channel (not legal advice), the limits of the record, and what the shift changes for organisations that hold data. items.title: How Perceived AI-Driven Personalization Is Associated with Online Purchase Intention in Tourism E-Commerce: A Moderated Sequential Mediation Model of Perceived Relevance and Trust in AI Recommendations
items.abstract: This study examines how perceived artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization is associated with online purchase intention in tourism e-commerce. It develops a moderated sequential mediation model in which perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations represent distinct evaluative pathways, while perceived AI response creativity and AI recommendation transparency condition different relationships within the proposed model. Data were collected from 871 consumers with recent experience using personalized recommendations on AI-enabled tourism platforms or travel assistants. Respondents were recruited through experience-based purposive sampling and screened to ensure direct and recallable experience with AI-generated travel recommendations. The proposed relationships were examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Perceived AI-driven personalization was positively associated with perceived recommendation relevance, trust in AI recommendations, and online purchase intention. Perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations were also positively associated with online purchase intention, while perceived recommendation relevance was positively related to trust in AI recommendations. Both constructs showed significant separate indirect associations between perceived AI-driven personalization and online purchase intention, and the theoretically ordered sequential indirect pathway was also statistically supported. Because the direct association remained significant and operated in the same direction as the indirect pathways, the observed statistical pattern was consistent with complementary partial mediation rather than evidence of a causal mediation mechanism. Perceived AI response creativity positively moderated the association between perceived AI-driven personalization and perceived recommendation relevance, whereas AI recommendation transparency positively moderated the association between perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations. The study distinguishes perceived AI-driven personalization from perceived recommendation relevance by treating the former as consumers’ assessment of adaptive recommendation tailoring and the latter as their judgment of recommendation–decision fit. It further conceptualizes perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations as distinct organism evaluations reflecting cognitive fit and reliance-oriented judgment, respectively. Creativity and transparency are positioned as relationship-specific boundary conditions rather than temporal stages, providing a more differentiated account of the theoretically ordered statistical pathways linking perceived AI-driven personalization with online purchase intention in tourism e-commerce.

items.abstract: Occupational safety and health (K3) is an important effort to protect employees from the risk of work accidents and occupational diseases, thereby supporting the achievement of optimal performance. However, cases of work accidents are still found every quarter at Rumah Sakit Islam Ibnu Sina Payakumbuh, such as needle-stick injuries, electric shocks, and direct contact exposure to patients with infectious diseases, which may affect employee performance. This study aimed to determine the relationship between occupational safety and health and employee performance at Rumah Sakit Islam Ibnu Sina Payakumbuh in 2026. This research used a quantitative method with a cross-sectional design. The population consisted of all employees of Rumah Sakit Islam Ibnu Sina Payakumbuh, totaling 224 people, with a sample of 144 respondents determined using the Slovin formula and proportionate stratified random sampling technique. Data were collected through questionnaires that had been tested for validity and reliability. Data analysis was carried out using univariate and bivariate analysis with the Chi-Square test at a significance level of 5%. The results showed that most respondents rated occupational safety and health as good, namely 74 respondents (51.4%), and employee performance as good, namely 75 respondents (52.1%). The Chi-Square test results obtained a p-value = 0.001 (<0.05), indicating a significant relationship between occupational safety and health and employee performance at Rumah Sakit Islam Ibnu Sina Payakumbuh in 2026. It can be concluded that the better the K3 implementation perceived by employees, the better their performance. Hospitals are expected to improve K3 implementation, particularly regarding human factors and tools and machinery factors, to support sustainable improvement in employee performance.

items.title: Image Dehazing as In-Context Tabular Inference
items.abstract: Image dehazing is traditionally addressed through handcrafted physical priors or task-specific deep learning models, often requiring carefully designed architectures or extensive model training. Recent advances in tabular foundation models (TFMs), however, offer an alternative learning paradigm in which continuous relationships can be inferred directly from contextual examples without task-specific model training. Motivated by this capability, this paper investigates whether single-image dehazing can be effectively reformulated as an in-context tabular regression problem and introduces DehazeTab, a framework that estimates atmospheric transmission from structured image-patch representations. Specifically, overlapping patches extracted from hazy images are transformed into tabular samples using handcrafted haze-related descriptors, pretrained visual embeddings, or their hybrid combinations, while corresponding transmission patches are summarized as scalar regression targets. A pretrained TFM then performs in-context regression using labeled reference patches to predict transmission values for unseen images without any further fine-tuning. These predictions are spatially aggregated into a transmission map, refined through guided filtering, and incorporated into the atmospheric scattering model to recover haze-free images. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate competitive restoration performance and reveal that physically motivated handcrafted features can outperform pretrained visual embeddings, while hybrid representations offer complementary benefits. Further analyses examine the effects of feature representations, patch selection, and contextual reference configurations on restoration quality. Beyond image dehazing, the findings highlight the potential of TFMs as an alternative paradigm for addressing low-level vision tasks through structured and in-context inference.

items.title: IMPACT OF AI ON THE HEALTH AND BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES OF YOUNGER GENERATION
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a significant part of the daily lives of the younger generation, influencing their education, and decision-making. Although AI provides several advantages, such as easy access to information, enhanced learning opportunities, and improved productivity, excessive use of AI may result in health problems and behavioural changes. Both primary and secondary data were used for the research purpose. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire, and responses of 100 has been considered. Secondary data were collected from journals and previously published research articles. Data were analysed using SPSS software. The study concludes that AI has a significant impact on the health and behavioural changes of the younger generation. Excessive AI usage has reduced face-to-face social interactions, increased dependency on AI, and contributed to physical health issues such as eye strain, tiredness, and reduced physical activity. Therefore, responsible and balanced use of AI is essential to promote the overall well-being of the younger generation.

items.title: IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE HUMAN ROLE IN THE FUTURE STOCK MARKET THEORETICAL AND IDEOLOGICAL EXPECTATIONS FOR UZBEKISTAN
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can reduce the cost of processing financial information, yet its contribution to stock market development depends on the institutions that govern data, decisions and accountability. This article examines that relationship for Uzbekistan through a critical synthesis of financial economics, research on human reliance on algorithms, international governance frameworks and national policy documents. It distinguishes established findings from conditional expectations and develops a framework in which automated analysis remains subject to accountable human authority. The central argument is that market quality depends on complementary investment in disclosure, professional competence and supervisory capacity. An ideological comparison identifies tensions between technological efficiency, developmental objectives and investor autonomy. Two analytical tables specify responsibilities and measurable criteria for future evaluation. The proposed framework yields testable propositions concerning disclosure quality, meaningful review and common dependence on model providers. For Uzbekistan, the defensible sequence begins with verified information and supervised analytical applications, followed by limited deployment only after independent validation. These conclusions are theoretical; the article reports no original trading experiment or estimated investment returns.

items.title: Impact of Digital Construction Technologies on Sustainability Awareness and Decision-Making in Civil Engineering Education
items.abstract: Digital technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), simulation platforms, and virtual and augmented reality are reshaping civil engineering education, yet their influence on sustainability awareness and decision-making is not well understood. This study surveyed 73 students enrolled in civil engineering courses at a public university in the southeastern United States. The instrument comprised 36 Likert-scale statements, grouped into eight constructs covering technology use in the curriculum, professional mindset, sustainability knowledge and lifecycle and environmental awareness. They also covered understanding of water resources, cognitive ability, emotional intelligence, and problem-solving. It also includes three decision scenarios in which a digital tool output conflicted with human input or practical constraints. Students reported favorable attitudes toward digital tools, along with strong conceptual sustainability awareness, but two applied-skill gaps stood out: only 32.9% felt able to interpret hydrologic models, and only 28.8% felt they could transfer simulation-based lessons to real world settings. In the scenarios, at most 12.3% of respondents accepted the digital output at face value, and 83.6% never did so across all three scenarios. Breadth of tool exposure was unrelated to perceptions or decision style, whereas the small group of students reporting exposure to hydrologic modeling rated their model interpretation ability substantially higher, suggesting that relevant depth matters more than the number of tools encountered. The findings support curricula that pair earlier and deeper BIM and hydrologic modeling instruction with lifecycle content and that train verification and interpretation skills alongside tool operation.

items.title: Impacts of AI-Role-Based Multimodal Takeover Messages and Affective State on Automated Driving Takeover Performance
items.abstract: Automated vehicles may still require drivers to resume control when system capability is exceeded. This study examined whether AI-role-framed takeover requests (TORs) and multisensory cues influence driver decision time under different affective states. Twenty-two licensed drivers completed 18 trials in a medium-fidelity SAE Level 3 driving simulator. A 3 × 3 × 2 within-subjects design manipulated AI role (Advisor, Co-pilot, Guardian), multisensory TOR condition (auditory + visual, auditory + tactile, auditory + olfactory), and affective state (positive valence/high arousal vs. negative valence/low arousal). Decision time and subjective ratings of satisfaction and usefulness were collected. Results showed significant main effects of AI role and multisensory condition on decision time. Co-pilot produced the longest decision time, while Guardian produced the shortest. Visual cues were associated with shorter decision times than tactile and olfactory cues. Affective state interacted with AI role. Subjective ratings showed no significant differences across conditions. Findings inform role-based, multisensory TOR design for automated vehicle systems.
