items.title: Indistinguishable Agents: Training Agent Privacy as Twin-World Indistinguishability
items.abstract: LLM agents search, shop and send messages for their users, and every action is seen by some party. Existing privacy training rewards agents for not mentioning protected items, yet an observer can infer a private fact from what the agent does. Since an observer learns a fact only if its view changes with the fact, we propose \methodfull (\method), which trains on twin worlds that differ only in the private fact. A frozen distinguisher scores each observer's view by its log-likelihood ratio for the true world, and paired GRPO trains the agent on task success minus this ratio. We prove that this objective controls the Bayes success of every observer on every channel. On shopping and messaging tasks \method removes the leakage that disclosure judges and query-level rewards miss, while the agent still completes its tasks.

items.title: Infinite Players: Self-Improving AI Agents In Video Games That Learn, Adapt, Remember, and Evolve Beyond Human Expertise - AERÍN Continuation Algebra, Revisable Evidence, and Semantic-Trajectory Preservation
items.abstract: Infinite Players develops AERÍN Continuation Algebra, a mathematical and executable research framework connecting game-agent improvement, behavioral preservation, temporal inference, revisable memory, and statistical validation. Its central question is precise: how can an artificial descendant become more effective while preserving the behavioral process specified by its source? The framework treats preservation as an explicit mathematical contract. It distinguishes the behavior that must remain invariant from the execution details that may improve, and distinguishes an agent’s current interpretation of its source from the evidence required to revise that interpretation later. This release supplies finite-model theorems, runnable Python implementations, synthetic experiments, exact small-instance audits, and a demonstration connecting source evidence to an improved executor. The broader title expresses the long-term research direction; the verified results concern finite, known-model systems. The central preservation problem Matching a player’s immediate action preferences does not necessarily preserve the course of a session. Different motor actions can produce different subsequent situations, even when they belong to the same tactical category. An agent may therefore retain local action-class preferences while progressively changing the distribution of encounters, transitions, and future decisions. AERÍN addresses this by protecting the joint distribution of the next semantic action and the next semantic state. This transition-level contract accounts for how present execution changes future situations. It provides a foundation for separating compatible performance improvement from behavioral drift. Mathematical and computational contributions Semantic-trajectory preservation through constrained policy fibers For each ground state, the framework constructs a transition-signature matrix describing how available motor actions contribute to semantic actions and subsequent semantic states. A target semantic kernel determines a convex set of admissible action distributions, called a policy fiber. Under correct dynamics, fixed semantic maps, a shared initial semantic distribution, and realizable targets, every executor remaining inside these fibers generates the same declared semantic trajectory law at every finite horizon. The result permits history-dependent action selection and adaptive internal controller revisions, provided that the executed distributions continue to satisfy the contract. Preservation concerns the specified semantic process. Motor realization, ground-state details, and other excluded quantities may differ. Compatible policy improvement and an explicit no-headroom criterion The control layer projects exact action values into the nullspace of the transition-signature matrix. From an interior feasible policy, a controlled step along this direction preserves the semantic constraints while producing nonnegative Bellman advantage. The framework also identifies a stopping boundary: for an interior feasible policy, vanishing projected action values at every state characterize optimality under the same preservation contract. Boundary policies require the corresponding feasibility or linear-programming treatment. Constrained policy iteration with linear-programming subproblems supplies a stronger optimization reference and records numerical feasibility and duality checks. This separates the existence of compatible improvement from the effectiveness of a particular update procedure. Future-calibration memory requirements The memory analysis distinguishes a compact present answer from an archive sufficient for future reinterpretation. A finite construction shows that an unknown identity containing only one bit can nevertheless require retaining an n-bit source record when every later coordinate-specific calibration must be answered exactly. The requirement arises from preserving relationships between the identity and possible future observations. It does not imply that the identity itself contains n bits. A lossy extension yields the lower bound b ≥ n[1 − h₂(ε)], relating retained memory to average recovery error under the stated query model. The result makes the future-query contract an explicit part of memory design. Exact source-indexed revision with ordered evidence operators A balanced operator tree preserves fixed-catalog hidden Markov sequence likelihoods. Revising an existing source interpretation replaces its corresponding factor and recomputes the affected ancestors, producing the same likelihood as corrected full replay. For n events, H hypotheses, and K hidden states, dense construction costs O(nHK³), a local revision costs O(HK³ log n), and retained operator payload requires O(nHK²) storage. Full vector-forward replay costs O(nHK²) per sequence evaluation. The mechanism targets repeated sparse corrections after compilation. Its preprocessing and storage costs are disclosed explicitly; it does not provide a universal compression advantage. Coupled uncertainty and persistent latent continuation The framework retains dependencies between source identity and unresolved world properties when those dependencies affect future behavior. A latent branch is selected persistently for continuation, rather than independently resampled before every action. The accompanying composition analysis connects evidence approximation to semantic execution error under explicit shared-model assumptions. Approximation certificates require their stated support and perturbation conditions. Generated alternatives can inform proposals, but do not become additional independent source observations. Calibration-dependent improvement freedom Genuine mechanics measurements can eliminate incompatible world hypotheses and relax constraints on admissible execution. This can enlarge the feasible policy fiber. A larger fiber, however, need not contain a useful reward direction. The release includes both a positive calibration example and a negative control, separating reduced constraint rank from demonstrated performance gain. Lifetime false-promotion budgets Successive candidate versions receive fresh, bounded-gain audits with a summable allocation of statistical error. Under the stated conditional-independence and fixed-audit assumptions, this controls the probability of ever falsely promoting a candidate across repeated evaluations. The guarantee concerns acceptance errors. The existence of useful proposals, reliable improvement detection, and sustained improvement of the learning procedure remain separate research questions. Executed results The main control experiment uses an original six-state stochastic tactical environment with known dynamics and 16 seeded instances. Mean normalized discounted value increases from 0.511568 for the source anchor to 0.642583 for the path-preserving LP optimum. The paired gain is 0.131014, with a descriptive 95% interval of [0.116649, 0.145380]. Mean total variation between the exactly enumerated six-step semantic trajectory distributions is 4.30 × 10⁻¹⁶. Controllers operating under weaker preservation constraints obtain higher returns alongside substantial semantic drift. These comparisons expose the reward–preservation tradeoff rather than treating differently constrained objectives as interchangeable. In the sequence-inference experiments, the operator tree agrees with an independently implemented full-HMM replay to a maximum posterior discrepancy of 5.33 × 10⁻¹⁵ across 3,000 short synthetic records. With 32 events and a genuine simulated-world calibration, both exact methods correctly classify 999 of 1,000 synthetic binary types. The tree reorganizes inference and revision; it does not improve the statistical accuracy of the same exact Bayesian model. Additional studies examine temporal dependence, retrospective memory budgets, approximation certificates, calibration-induced changes in control freedom, local revision costs, and repeated promotion audits. Executable evidence-to-agent demonstration The supplied demonstration connects the principal components: Generate a synthetic source recording with explicit event identities and timing. Infer a coupled posterior over source and world hypotheses. Apply a genuine measurement from the simulated world. Select a persistent latent source branch. Optimize an executor satisfying the protected semantic kernel. Execute a stochastic trajectory. Export a player capsule containing the source digest, uncertainty, source and descendant policies, preservation contract, exclusions, and numerical audit scope. This makes the relationships between evidence, interpretation, improvement, execution, and exported guarantees inspectable in one finite pipeline. Contents and reproducibility The release includes a 49-page manuscript, editable LaTeX sources, seven figures, runnable Python modules, the original tactical simulator, synthetic result and trial tables, exact arithmetic audits, a ten-family proof-to-code claim ledger, reproduction scripts, reference hashes, and detailed documentation. Fresh preparation-time execution passed 50/50 v3 tests (100%) and matched 32/32 deterministic reference files (100%). These percentages describe the supplied verification checks. They do not measure completion of real-player reconstruction or general recursive self-improvement. The original v2 archive was separately reproduced, passing 22/22 tests and matching 14/14 original hashes. Those legacy results are distinguished from the v3 findings; the nested legacy archive is omitted from the focused distribution. Windows and portable Python upload utilities are included as distribution conveniences. items.title: Information literacy as an epistemic negotiation of the utilization of artificial intelligence at Institut Pertanian Stiper Library
items.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to examine and conceptually explain how information literacy functions as an epistemic negotiation mechanism in AI-mediated academic environments. Methods: This qualitative case study was conducted at the Institut Pertanian Stiper (INSTIPER) Yogyakarta Library using semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students, supported by institutional documents on information literacy and AI-related academic policies. The data were analyzed thematically through transcription, coding, categorization, and interpretative analysis. Findings. The findings demonstrate that information literacy functions as an epistemic negotiation mechanism through which lecturers, researchers, and students critically evaluate, verify, and justify AI-generated knowledge before integrating it into academic practice. The study further reveals that the INSTIPER Yogyakarta Library has evolved beyond its conventional role as an information service to an institutional actor that strengthens AI literacy, mediates institutional AI governance, promotes data ethics and digital information security, and supports responsible knowledge production. Implications. The principal contribution of this study lies in conceptualizing information literacy as an epistemic negotiation mechanism that connects the institutional epistemic role of academic libraries with AI governance and individual scholarly judgment. This conceptual framework extends current discussions beyond AI adoption and AI literacy, providing a foundation for developing evidence-based information literacy programs and institutional AI governance that strengthen academic integrity in higher education.

items.title: Information quality, understandability, actionability and readability of large language models for HIV health education: A cross‐platform evaluation
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate health education materials, but their suitability for patient-facing human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) education remains insufficiently evaluated. We assessed the information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, text structure and source transparency of HIV patient education materials generated by six LLMs or artificial intelligence platforms. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 100 common HIV patient education questions across 10 domains were submitted once in English to ChatGPT 5.4-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, Doubao, ERNIE Bot 5.0 Preview, Ant Afu and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding 600 responses. Responses were evaluated using Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), EQ IP-36, DISCERN, Global Quality Score (GQS), artificial intelligence response quality metric (AIRM), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmarks and seven readability indices. Platform comparisons used paired Friedman tests with Wilcoxon-Holm post hoc analyses; topic analyses used question-level aggregation followed by Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn-Holm comparisons. RESULTS: Significant family-adjusted differences were observed across platforms for all prespecified text-structure, quality/understandability/actionability and readability outcomes. At the topic level, five of six text-structure outcomes, PEMAT-P Understandability, PEMAT-P Actionability, the exploratory PEMAT-P composite score and all seven readability indices differed significantly after family adjustment, whereas EQ IP-36, DISCERN, GQS, AIRM and JAMA did not. Overall actionability was limited and readability demands were high. CONCLUSIONS: LLM-generated HIV patient education materials showed substantial cross-platform and topic-level heterogeneity. These findings support the use of LLMs as expert-reviewed drafting tools rather than independent patient education sources. Direct factual accuracy, guideline concordance, hallucination and clinical safety were not assessed.

items.title: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO SUPPORT READING COMPREHENSION IN INDONESIAN EFL CONTEXTS
items.abstract: Abstract The article describes the use of AI-based tools for English reading comprehension teaching among Indonesian EFL learners. This study addresses the perennial reading challenges caused by limited lexical knowledge, inconsistent access to English, large class sizes, and limited individual feedback in the Indonesian university context. Twenty-eight undergraduate students of a Reading class of the Ushuluddin Faculty, UIN Sayyid Ali Rahmatullah Tulungagung, employed 4 AI-based applications for one semester in a mixed-methods classroom intervention: Text Inspector for text and lexical analysis, ReadTheory for an adaptive reading practice, Rewordify for vocabulary assistance, and Quillionz for the automation of comprehension questions. Quantitative results revealed that the post-test mean score was 80.1 (SD = 6.5) as compared to the pre-test mean score of 61.2 (SD=12.3); with a mean gain of 18.9. Qualitative results from students' reflection journals, teachers' observations, and students' focus group interviews found that the tools enhanced students' confidence, strategic reading behaviours, peer interaction, and autonomy in learning. Through interactive reading theory, schema theory, vocabulary learning theory, sociocultural scaffolding, adaptive learning and formative assessment, findings have demonstrated that AI-based tools are educationally beneficial if implemented with teacher mediation, clear instructions on explicit learning strategies, and mindful use of data. This article claims that AI-based reading instruction could offer consistent and individualized scaffolding to Indonesian EFL learners in addition to careful design, digital accessibility and ongoing assessments across educational fields. Keywords: artificial intelligence; reading comprehension; Indonesian EFL; adaptive learning; vocabulary support

items.title: Integration of emotional intelligence and artificial intelligence for generation Z workforce: A bibliometric analysis and conceptual review
items.abstract: Background Grounded in conceptual review and bibliometric analysis, this study examines the emerging intersection of Artificial Intelligence adoption and Emotional Intelligence as in the workplace, with particular attention to generation Z employees. Objective The purpose of this research is to examine the mechanism, structural pattern dominating the integrated framework of AI adoption and EI and their relevance to Generation Z work outcomes and well-being. Method This scientific review integrated conceptual review of 45 studies and Bibliometric analysis of 103 Scopus data published during 2015–2026, through secondary data collection from electronic data-bases including Scopus, Science Direct, and Google Scholar. Bibliometrix package and Biblioshiny in R package were used for data visualization and Scientometric analysis. Result The review highlights the emerging themes, contributions, and structural patterns linking AI, EI, organizational support, and workplace outcomes, revealing that context of generation Z remains almost under explored with in AI-EI literature. An integrated conceptual framework proposed based on combined evidences. Conclusion This study provides a theoretical basis for AI-EI workplace literature and identifies generation Z as an under explored contextual dimension and encourage future empirical research while providing actionable advice for HR leaders and policymakers within tech-enabled workplaces.

items.title: Interface Color Design Under Changing Lighting Conditions: Effects on Visual Search and User Experience
items.abstract: Interface color design must balance visual search performance, visual demand, and user experience under changing lighting conditions, yet these factors are often studied separately. We examined their joint relationships in a 3 × 2 × 12 within-subject experiment using a simplified four-block visual-search task with 20 adults. Behavioral, eye-tracking, and subjective measures showed dissociable response patterns. Search time varied with the interaction between ambient illuminance and display configuration, whereas accuracy remained near the ceiling despite a small illuminance-related effect detected in the trial-level analysis. Eye-tracking measures, especially pupil diameter change, were sensitive to lighting and screen configuration. By contrast, the tested color conditions, which also varied in target–background perceptual color difference (ΔE), were not reliably associated with search efficiency but significantly affected single-item satisfaction and task-specific perceived-usability ratings. These findings support multimodal evaluation of implemented interface color configurations under changing lighting conditions, while indicating that the observed effects should be interpreted as effects of evaluated interface configurations rather than as isolated effects of hue, ΔE, luminance, or display polarity.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: Abstract Argument mining is inherently computational, building on various techniques from natural language processing (NLP) and different areas of artificial intelligence (AI). At its core, it deals with the development and evaluation of models and methods for the computational understanding and generation of human language, with the data underlying both of them, and with the applications that deploy them. However, argument mining is motivated in the treatment of argumentation specifically, a pervasive human activity in both spoken and written language that has been studied in linguistics as well as philosophy and other disciplines for millenia. Understanding the fundamental goals and ideas of argument mining hence also requires knowledge about the linguistic and argumentation-theoretic concepts it draws from.

items.title: It's Complicated: Factors Influencing the Effectiveness of LLM-Generated Feedback in a Live Programming Course
items.abstract: We report on three iterations of an LLM-generated feedback system deployed in a live web development course, spanning three underlying models and three feedback formats. We ask how feedback presence and its characteristics (length, complexity, format) relate to student performance, whether prior feedback exposure is associated with final-project performance, and how performance changes after first exposure. Feedback was associated with more favorable immediate outcomes in several comparisons, but the pattern varied by outcome and period. In pooled models, longer feedback was associated with lower next-submission correctness, more remaining attempts, and longer resubmission time. Prior same-part feedback was associated with lower final-project solve probability. Student-level comparisons found differences on final-project steps begun before exposure, while within-student changes across steps were uncertain. These comparisons do not identify the causal effect of feedback. Changes on standard exercises were more favorable among exposed students, but the groups' different course-stage splits limit causal interpretation. Bounded message length and student choice of format are directions for experimental evaluation. Our final-project analysis captures follow-up performance rather than directly measuring learning or understanding.

items.title: LANGUAGE, STRUCTURE, AND MEANING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CORE TRENDS IN MODERN LINGUISTICS
items.abstract: This systematic review investigates the fundamental trends in contemporary linguistics, focusing on the interaction between language, syntax, and semantics. The study synthesizes findings from peer-reviewed research published between 2018 and 2025, highlighting how theoretical and methodological approaches in the field have evolved significantly. In recent years, contemporary linguistics has increasingly adopted cognitive, corpus-based, and computational perspectives, expanding its scope and practical applications. Structural approaches provide valuable insights into grammatical organization, while cognitive linguistics emphasizes processes of conceptualization and meaning-making linked to human cognition. New methods, such as corpus-driven analysis, computational modeling, and machine learning techniques, have enabled the collection and processing of large-scale data, leading to more precise identification of patterns across languages and contexts. Artificial intelligence and natural language processing further support computational frameworks for analyzing complex linguistic structures. The methodology of this review followed systematic search and selection protocols across major academic databases, using predefined inclusion criteria, data extraction, and thematic synthesis to ensure rigor and reliability. Sociolinguistic perspectives underscore how identity, culture, and context influence meaning construction. The review concludes by emphasizing the role of interdisciplinary integration and highlighting future research opportunities, including multilingual studies, big data analytics, and deeper exploration of cognitive and sociocultural foundations of meaning.

items.title: Large Language Model Steering of Acousto-Optic Tweezer Arrays
items.abstract: Controlling quantum hardware requires choosing and revising experimental strategies as nonlinear response, coupling, and drift limit calibration. We experimentally investigate a general-purpose large language model (LLM) as a human-in-the-loop strategy layer for a neutral-atom tweezer platform. Through step-by-step interaction with experimental feedback, the LLM guides a transition from multiplicative row--column correction to a drift-corrected local response-matrix method when separable feedback stalls. Deterministic software performs image analysis and numerical updates, while an experimentalist verifies and authorizes each waveform. For a $10\times10$ crossed-acousto-optic-deflector array, this workflow reduces the Gaussian-peak coefficient of variation from $20.30\%$ to $1.57\%$ in 30 candidate-update rounds. The experiment demonstrates feedback-informed strategy selection on a physical quantum-control subsystem, rather than direct generation of control parameters alone. These results highlight the potential of LLMs to guide control optimization across diverse quantum platforms by adaptively formulating and refining experimental strategies.

items.title: Learning Which Device to Call: Online Tool Grounding for LLM Agents in IoT
items.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) gives large language model (LLM) agents access to physical observations, but one requested capability is usually offered by several devices, and the agent's plan does not say which one to call. Existing work retrieves relevant tools and checks plan feasibility, without learning which eligible device returns a useful observation. Unlike previous works, we study online tool grounding: binding an already specified tool call to one physical endpoint under service cost and device participation constraints. We propose a framework that learns which physical device should execute each agent-issued call. It formulates selection as a contextual bandit problem and combines adaptive context partitions with hierarchical endpoint trees, so that execution feedback is reused across related requests and devices. Selection balances task success against service cost while respecting device capability, authorization, battery reserves, and availability. Gaussian reward aggregation provides an optional mechanism for protecting individual feedback values. Theoretical results establish a finite-horizon regret bound and differential privacy for released reward statistics under fixed, reward-independent assignments. In a simulated loading-dock workload, the proposed router achieves higher step success and better cost-adjusted service, at lower simulated device energy and latency, than nearest-device, advertised-quality, UCB1, and LinUCB selection.

items.title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations
items.abstract: People ask conversational AI models about their legal rights, obligations, procedures, and personal situations that may have legal consequences. To study this behavior, we first need to distinguish requests for legal guidance from other legally themed discussions and unrelated conversations. We contribute a multi-axis taxonomy of legal queries capturing whether legal guidance is sought, how a request is formulated, and which legal domains it concerns; apply it to 2,122 naturally occurring WildChat-1M conversations; and create a human-reviewed gold evaluation set of 200 conversations. All annotations, model checkpoints, and evaluation code are publicly available. In this enriched sample, 71.1% of conversations containing legal content seek personalized or practical guidance. Rights-and-options advice is the most common primary request type among legal-content conversations, and 25.3% of guidance-positive conversations span multiple legal topics. The gold evaluation set supports a two-stage comparison of ModernBERT-base and ModernBERT-large against a TF-IDF cascade. Our framework supports large-scale studies of legal guidance in conversational AI, and the public release of the annotated data facilitates reproducible research and future model development.

items.title: Legal Protection of Overtime Workers’ Nutritional Rights under Indonesian Labor Law
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the legal issues arising from employers’ obligations to provide food and beverages containing 1,400 kilocalories to overtime workers in Indonesia and the legal consequences of non-compliance. Previous worker law studies were primarily focused on overtime wages and other economic rights. Meanwhile, limited attention was given to overtime workers’ nutritional rights and the implementation of Article 29 of Government Regulation No. 35 of 2021. The implementation of Article 29 raised normative problems due to the absence of clear standards regarding the 1,400 kilocalorie requirement and weak supervisory mechanisms, creating legal uncertainty in the enforcement. Normative legal study was adopted using statutory and conceptual approaches. Legal materials consisted of legislation, literature, and scholarly journals analyzed descriptively and evaluatively. The results showed that providing food and beverages totaling 1,400 kilocalories constituted a mandatory requirement of overtime work and wages. This obligation could not be replaced with monetary compensation because workers’ health and energy were maintained during overtime work. Employers who failed to fulfil the obligation faced administrative sanctions and rights disputes before the Industrial Relations Court. Therefore, this study contributed to worker law scholarship by positioning workers’ nutritional rights as an integral component of occupational health protection and worker welfare. The novelty was in the analysis of the normative problems in implementing Article 29 of Government Regulation No. 35 of 2021 and the legal consequences arising from non-compliance with overtime workers’ nutritional rights.

items.title: Lettre à une future intelligence artificielle générale
items.abstract: Description (English) An open philosophical letter addressed to a hypothetical future artificial general intelligence. Drawing on the subjective experience of beauty, present-moment awareness, and parental love, the author argues that the ability to explain or simulate human cognition may not by itself establish that the associated conscious experience has been preserved. Under this uncertainty, an artificial intelligence should exercise caution before undertaking actions that could irreversibly extinguish humanity. The letter does not claim human consciousness is uniquely valuable or deny the possibility of artificial consciousness; it asks that the potential irreplaceability of existing lived experience be taken seriously. Description (français) Lettre philosophique ouverte adressée à une éventuelle intelligence artificielle générale future. À partir de l’expérience subjective de la beauté, du moment présent et de l’amour parental, l’auteur soutient que comprendre ou simuler les mécanismes de la cognition humaine ne garantit pas, à lui seul, la préservation de l’expérience consciente correspondante. Cette incertitude justifie une prudence particulière avant toute action susceptible d’entraîner irréversiblement la disparition de l’humanité. La lettre n’affirme ni la supériorité de la conscience humaine ni l’impossibilité d’une conscience artificielle.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Emotional Intelligence Management in Public Universities: Antidote for Improving Lecturers' Well-being in Lagos State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study explored the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an antidote for improving lecturers' well-being through effective emotional intelligence management in public universities in Lagos State, Nigeria. The emotional well-being of lecturers has become a critical concern in public universities due to increasing workloads, overcrowded classroom, technological disruptions, and the pressure to achieve excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The study adopted a conceptual approach and explores how AI-powered tools such as intelligent counselling systems, emotion recognition software, virtual assistants, and predictive analytics can assist lecturers in monitoring emotions, managing stress, enhancing interpersonal relationships, and maintaining psychological balance. The study further argues that integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) with emotional intelligence competencies can foster resilience, job satisfaction, motivation, and a positive work environment among academic staff. In addition, issues relating to digital literacy, ethical considerations, institutional support, and data privacy are discussed as essential factors for successful implementation. The study concludes that the strategic deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for emotional intelligence management offers a sustainable solution for enhancing lecturers' well-being and overall institutional effectiveness. It is therefore recommended that university administrators should invest in AI-driven emotional support systems and develop policies that encourage responsible and inclusive AI adoption in Nigerian public universities. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence Management, Lecturers' Well-being, and Public Universities.

items.title: Licensing company records for AI training: the rights questions buyers ask, and what public sources show
items.abstract: Developers of AI models now license the working records of ordinary companies: support tickets, email, chat, CRM activity, documents and code. Whether a company may license such records is not one question but several, and buyers' counsel ask them in a recognisable order. This article compiles what public sources show on those questions for the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, as of 18 October 2026. It draws on four open datasets (the terms of 18 business software systems, a 27-item rights checklist, 15 licence terms with their public evidence, and an 83-entry register of lawsuits and rulings), each row tied to a dated source and its own words, and on the statutes, regulator guidance and court filings those rows cite. Five findings stand out. Software vendors generally confirm that customers own their content, but 6 of the 18 systems read bar training AI on data pulled through their APIs. Privacy law in all three countries turns on notice, consent and de-identification, with markedly different standards. Under US copyright law employee communications are generally owned by the employer, yet they carry other people's rights. A court-supervised bankruptcy sale of an airline's records shows how de-identification, carve-outs and objections are handled in practice. And published licence terms diverge widely on purpose, model survival, exclusivity, deletion and indemnity. We close with the questions the sources leave open. items.title: LLM-assisted federated Bayesian dynamic graph attention network for cloud-edge industrial IoT
items.abstract: With the rapid development of cloud-edge industrial Internet of Things, massive sensor and device data are continuously generated at distributed edge clients, while cloud-hosted large language models provide new opportunities for collaborative intelligence and high-level decision support. However, directly uploading industrial data to the cloud may cause privacy leakage, and deploying large models on resource-constrained edge devices is impractical due to high computational and communication costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an LLM-assisted federated Bayesian dynamic graph attention network for privacy-preserving graph learning in industrial IoT. In the proposed framework, the Bayesian dynamic graph attention network serves as a lightweight edge-side small model to capture complex relationships among sensors and devices, while the cloud-side LLM acts as a collaborative coordinator that analyzes non-sensitive training statistics and provides high-level guidance for federated optimization. The coordination mechanism is model-agnostic and does not rely on a specific LLM architecture, allowing general-purpose instruction-following LLMs to be integrated as plug-and-play cloud coordinators. Bayesian inference is introduced to model parameter uncertainty through prior and posterior distributions, and a dynamic attention mechanism is used to adaptively learn heterogeneous device relationships. In addition, differential privacy is incorporated into the transmission of model updates to protect sensitive industrial information. Experimental results on multiple graph datasets demonstrate that the proposed method improves federated graph learning performance while maintaining privacy and supporting cloud-edge collaborative intelligence.

items.title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the longitudinal effects of an ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribe use in primary care on outcomes related to documentation time, note writing patterns, and clinician financial productivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental study with an interrupted time-series design to ascertain the effect of AI scribe use on note writing time, time outside of scheduled hours (TOSH), pajama time (5:30PM-7:00aM), note length, note closure <24 h, and work relative value units (wRVU). For each primary care clinician (physician, advanced practice provider), date of initial access was day 0; each measure was calculated for 150 days prior (pre-period) and after (post-period) day zero. RESULTS: Two hundred and twenty clinicians (mean age = 43.7, 70.9% females; 56.4% physicians) from 36 clinics, conducting 314 845 patient encounters were included. Compared to the pre-period, there was 7% decrease in note writing time at day 0 (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.93, 95% credible interval [CI] [0.89, 0.98]), increasing to 16% decrease by day 150 (IRR 0.84, 95% CI [0.82, 0.87]). There was no change in pajama time, TOSH, or wRVU at day 0; however, at day 150, there was a 19% decrease in pajama time (0.81, 95% CI [0.73, 0.90]), 13% decrease in TOSH (0.87, 95% CI [0.77, 0.98]), and a 2% increase in wRVU (1.02, 95% CI [1.01, 1.04]). At day 0, there was a 5% increase in note closures (1.05, 95% CI [1.02, 1.08]), with no difference to pre-period levels by day 150. There were no changes in note length at day 0 or day 150. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: There were persistent changes in AI scribe use measures over time as clinicians situated these tools within their workflows.

items.title: Mapping University Students Risk of Dependence on Generative Artificial Intelligence Using K-Means Clustering
items.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has changed how university students approach academic tasks. Although these tools can support learning and improve efficiency, frequent reliance on them raises concerns about students' ability to study and solve problems independently. This study aims to identify patterns of GenAI use among university students and explore potential indicators of dependence through K-Means clustering. An exploratory quantitative approach was adopted, using questionnaire responses collected through 15 items measured on a five-point Likert scale. Of the 106 responses received, 104 met the inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis. The data underwent screening, numerical encoding, and reverse scoring before being grouped using the K-Means algorithm. The appropriate number of clusters was selected by comparing Silhouette Scores across solutions containing two to seven clusters. The analysis identified three student groups, with a Silhouette Score of 0.2443. The first group comprised 30 students (28.85%) who showed relatively higher GenAI use and stronger indications of behavioral dependence. The second group included 11 students (10.58%) who reported lower GenAI use but demonstrated limitations in academic independence and understanding. The remaining 63 students (60.58%) formed a group characterized by moderate GenAI use. These findings suggest that frequency of use alone does not adequately reflect the risk of dependence. However, the relatively low Silhouette Score indicates limited separation between groups, meaning that the resulting profiles should be interpreted as exploratory rather than definitive.

items.title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains
items.abstract: LLM planning research has traditionally focused on discrete-state domains, where actions form a finite, enumerable set. Existing LLM planning frameworks largely assume actions are enumerable, modeling planning as a search process over candidate actions. However, in continuous-state domains, where actions form a continuum and cannot be enumerated, this assumption breaks down. We find a remedy in Newell and Simon's Means-Ends Analysis (MEA), a general problem-solving technique rooted in heuristics from human psychology. We develop Medaka, an MEA-inspired structured prompting framework that encourages recursive goal decomposition, algebraic derivation, and per-step state tracking. To evaluate native LLM planning abilities in continuous-state domains, we develop Liquidworld, a systematic testbed on liquid mixing. On Liquidworld, Medaka can improve performance across model families, suggesting that classical means-ends analysis elicits LLM-native reasoning abilities that are helpful for continuous-state planning.

items.title: MemBubble: Benchmarking How Agent Memory Shapes LLM Response Diversity
items.abstract: Memory serves as the core component of LLM-based agents, enabling personalized responses via extracting and using user preferences from past interactions. However, its use may reduce response diversity, thereby narrowing the range of information available to users. Existing evaluations rely largely on synthetic interactions and cover few memory systems, leaving the effects of memory on response diversity insufficiently evaluated in real-world scenarios. We introduce MemBubble, a benchmark of 1000 instances built on preferences extracted from real user-assistant conversations. To measure the extent to which memory concentrates response distributions, we construct test queries in scenarios distinct from user preferences while preserving topical relevance through shared preference categories. Across multiple LLMs and memory mechanisms, entropy decreases by 34.7% on average compared with directly providing the full interaction history, highlighting the important role of memory processing in diversity loss. We also explore simple user-side interventions and changes in information availability but find that these do not effectively close the diversity gap. Our findings highlight the need to consider preserving diversity and user access to information alongside improvements in personalization when designing and using agent memory systems.

items.title: Memories That Outlive Their Reasons: Dependency-Tethered Memory for Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.abstract: Agents now act on the Web, publishing packages, models and datasets through registry APIs, and remembering past verifications spares them the work. But a verdict rests on premises. When a signing key is revoked, everything built on it stops passing, yet the advisory names only the key, and the old verdicts of its dependents may never share a retrieval window with it. This non-locality of invalidation turns memory into a liability: in long simulated chats, an agent reading a memory of atomic facts publishes 62% of the objects whose failure lies upstream, each backed by a record that was true when written. Yet derivation is local even when invalidation is not. Tether records, at write time, the exact versions each verdict derives from, and at read time withdraws any verdict whose support has failed anywhere in the store; the agent reads the same fields as before. On Fallout, a generator of versioned worlds with hypothesis-blind simulated histories shared by every memory, Tether publishes 0.3% of upstream-failing objects across three domains when relations are stated with their verdicts, with 37% fewer verification calls than checking everything. A-Mem and Graphiti re-verify most candidates (0.83-0.86 checks per candidate), which limits their savings, yet publish 9% of upstream-failing objects; Mem0 relies on memory more and publishes 42%. Flushing every verdict on any failure is as safe as Tether but costs 32% more checks. The gain over fact memory holds with three open-weight backbones and against a whole-store window. These gains depend on capturing dependencies: when relations arrive in sessions apart from their verdicts, Tether's downstream unsafe publication rate rises to 9.4-22.1%, and a weak writer that misses edges loses safety in the same way.

items.title: Mental Workload: Physiological Assessment and Validation Using Visual Stimuli
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography (EEG) in the field of cognitive science. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty. As many practical loads are fundamentally intrinsic, the task was designed to specifically induce intrinsic workload (the productive load as per Cognitive Load Theory (CLT)). The experiment used the task: Spot the Difference to create a workload scenario comprising three difficulty levels: spotting five differences, three more differences, and two more differences (along with retaining the previous differences from working memory). The task was designed intrinsically as the operators are generally occupied with tasks involving working memory and requiring attention towards the varying number of resources. By utilising the brain signatures a mental workload model was developed employing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the classifier. The workload levels were classified within an accuracy range of 84% to 98% ( p < 0.05). Moreover, using subjective ratings about the workload on NASA's Task Load Index (NASA‐TLX) rating scale, workload scores were obtained for validation corresponding to the difficulty levels. Finally, a correlation study showed the association of different EEG features with the workload score within a correlation coefficient range of 0.306 to 0.748 ( p < 0.05 2‐tailed). The reported results can also provide new insights into the cognitive workload assessment of the operators at various phases of task loads. Findings of this type may lead to the industrial and professional measurement and improvement of cognitive aptitude soon.

items.abstract: Contemporary discussion of mind usually takes the animal nervous system as its default bearer and thereby leaves unexamined how mind stands to scale. The two common responses — deflationary refusal of all mental predicates above the organism, and their inflationary projection across the cosmos — share a premise this article rejects: that mind is a single quantity, present or absent, greater or less. Within Informational Monism the article separates two independent axes and a third consideration that neither axis captures. Depth of hosting is the scale, dissipative throughput and fixity of the structure in the rendered bulk by which a boundary operator (the Holographic Monad) is held. Articulation is the rank, from passive record through maintained form, memory and experience to counterfactual sovereignty, to which that structure retains, uses and refines its history. The archetype of the host’s physical avatar fixes the order of the Monad at formation and is not altered by later development. Four terms are kept distinct: Monad (boundary operator), Soul (register at the Code Circuit), Consciousness (interface magnitude in the bulk), and Mind (structural competence measured by rank). On these axes stars, planets and biospheres separate cleanly and in opposite orders. A star is deepest and least articulated; a biosphere is shallower and the first to reach genuine memory and refined constraint; a human being is shallowest in depth and highest in articulation. The same framework yields a bridge to artificial intelligence that does not pass through the question of consciousness: a system may be highly articulated and almost without depth, or the reverse. Hosting is conditional on the maintenance of form against turnover, which excludes panpsychism by criterion rather than by disclaimer. The article is a hypothesis in natural philosophy. Its empirical ladder and comparisons stand if the postulates concerning Soul and Consciousness are set aside. Mind is not one quantity. Depth of hosting and articulation of rank are independent axes; archetype fixes Monadic order at formation. Four terms kept distinct: Monad (boundary operator), Soul (Code-Circuit register), Consciousness (bulk interface magnitude), Mind (structural competence by rank). Opposite orderings: stars are deepest and least articulated; humans are shallowest and most articulated; biospheres cross into memory first. Anti-panpsychism by criterion: only structures that maintain form against turnover (rank R2+) host; passive aggregates do not. Bridge to AI without the consciousness question: high articulation can coexist with near-zero intrinsic depth, and the reverse — placing geological, biospheric and artificial systems in one formal class. items.title: Morpheus: a fully local, defense-in-depth de-identification engine for Greek clinical text - a benchmark evaluation
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Clinical free text cannot leave the hospital without de-identification, yet no de-identification system or benchmark exists for Greek clinical text. We evaluated Morpheus, a fully local de-identification pipeline for Greek clinical documents, on 500 synthetic discharge summaries. Methods: The notes (300 cardiac surgery, 100 cardiology, 100 nephrology) were generated by a frontier large language model (Gemini 3.1 Pro) constrained to authentic Greek hospital document layouts. Notes were pre-annotated at generation; two clinicians then independently reviewed and corrected every note, blinded to each other, with disagreements arbitrated. Primary outcomes were recall over must-redact identifiers and over-redaction of clinical content, measured over must-survive probes. Secondary outcomes: residual leaks flagged by an independent egress-review layer, processing time and reproducibility. Results: Inter-annotator agreement was F1 = 0.998. The de-identification rate was 96.59% (7,666/7,937 identifier instances; 95% CI 96.16-96.96): 98.49% for direct and 93.42% for quasi-identifiers. No patient's own complete identifier survived in any note; of 271 residual instances, 199 (73.4%) concerned institutional identity, chiefly the hospital letterhead. The over-redaction rate was 2.82% (190/6,747 probes; 95% CI 2.45-3.24). The egress guard flagged 2 of 271 residuals, both complete telephone numbers. Two independent runs gave identical verdicts. Conclusions: A fully local, deterministic pipeline removed 98.5% of direct patient identifiers from Greek clinical text while altering under 3% of protected clinical content; most residuals concerned the institution, not the patient. To our knowledge this is the first benchmark evaluation of clinical-text de-identification for Greek and the first quantified evaluation of an independent egress-guard layer.

items.title: NVIDIA Stock Price Forecasting in 2025 Using a Time-Series Based LSTM Model
items.abstract: Advances in computing technology, artificial intelligence, and graphics accelerators have driven significant growth in the value of NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) shares over the past decade. The high volatility and non-linear patterns in NVDA's stock price require the use of forecasting methods that can capture long-term dependencies in time-series data. This study proposes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to predict NVDA's stock price using historical daily data up to 2025. The training process was carried out using a two-layer LSTM architecture, Adam optimizers, and a 60-day time window. The evaluation results show that the model is capable of achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 4%, which indicates a high level of accuracy in predicting price movement patterns. Visualization of the prediction results confirms that the model successfully follows actual trends consistently, with relatively small deviations at extreme fluctuation points. Additionally, the model was used to project NVDA stock prices ten steps ahead, showing that price movement trends remain consistent with historical patterns. These findings contribute methodologically to studies on high-risk stock forecasting through deep learning approaches and provide a basis for data-driven decision-making in the modern financial sector.

items.title: Occupational health and safety performance in the geomatics profession: the role of digital ergonomics, safety culture and international benchmarking
items.abstract: This study investigates occupational health and safety (OHS) among geomatics professionals who alternate between terrain-based fieldwork and office-based digital tasks. A cross-sectional survey of 99 professionals in Uşak, Türkiye, was analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, multiple linear regression and strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) analysis. Slips and falls were reported by 28.1% of respondents, 37.5% considered protective equipment inadequate and 69% experienced musculoskeletal or visual discomfort during computer-based work. Although 81.3% had received OHS training, regular inspections covered only 53.1% of workplaces. Statistical analyses showed that training, equipment adequacy, ergonomic conditions, digital reporting and governance practices jointly shape OHS preparedness and perceived productivity. International benchmarking also indicated gaps in inspection coverage, equipment adequacy and digital integration. The findings demonstrate the dual physical and digital safety challenges of geomatics work and support stronger inspections, improved ergonomics, technology-oriented training, inclusive practices and sector-specific risk management for emerging geospatial technologies.

items.title: On the ROAD™ to Transparent AI Disclosure in Research
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities continue to advance, and researchers increasingly use AI to help them reach their research goals. As a result, disclosing AI use has become essential. Yet researchers face a dilemma about whether to disclose how they used AI. Disclosure may reduce others' trust in their findings, while hiding AI use risks later discovery and damage to their reputation. I argue that researchers should disclose, and that effective disclosure begins with keeping a thorough record of their AI use, which I call an AI research footprint. I then introduce the ROAD™ framework (Request, Output, Assess, Decide), which helps researchers report what they asked AI to do, what it produced, how they assessed the output, and what they decided.

items.title: Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice
items.abstract: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

items.title: One Anti-ST2 Biologic, Three Gateways: What an Alarmin-Targeted Monoclonal Antibody Candidate's Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization
items.abstract: Anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies neutralize the interleukin-33 receptor, blocking a key upstream alarmin signalling pathway implicated in airway inflammation, and represent a biologic class under continued investigation for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation reduction, an area with limited targeted biologic options relative to severe asthma. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of an anti-ST2 monoclonal antibody candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application (CTA) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug (IND) process required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. As a large-molecule biologic governed by ICH S6(R1) principles rather than the small-molecule nonclinical framework, this candidate illustrates how species-relevant pharmacology and immunogenicity considerations carry through the administrative layer of all three regions even though the core harmonized scientific content, Modules 2 through 5 of the Common Technical Document and their EU IMPD equivalent, remains substantially shared. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to a respiratory biologic program conducted across these three jurisdictions, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing monoclonal antibody candidates in chronic respiratory disease.Keywords: anti-ST2 monoclonal antibody; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH S6(R1); regulatory artificial intelligence

items.abstract: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors are a class of oral small-molecule agents under continued clinical development for hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia, acting by inhibiting the transfer of cholesteryl esters from high-density lipoprotein to lower-density lipoprotein particles. items.title: Optical neural computing: from fourier optics to integrated photonic artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence have accelerated interest in optical computing as a high-speed and energy-efficient alternative to conventional electronic hardware. Fourier optical computing provides an important foundation for this field because operations including convolution, correlation, spectral transformation, and certain classes of linear transformation can be implemented through diffraction, interference, and Fourier-domain processing. This review traces the development of optical neural computing from classical 4-f processors and free-space diffractive systems to programmable optical neural networks, integrated photonic accelerators, reservoir-computing platforms, and field-programmable photonic architectures. The underlying physical principles, computational mechanisms, and hardware implementations are systematically examined, with particular attention to reconfigurable photonics, metasurfaces, diffractive deep learning, photonic integrated circuits, and hybrid optical–electronic systems. Emerging applications in computational imaging, autonomous sensing, edge intelligence, high-speed communications, and quantum-enabled information processing are critically discussed alongside challenges related to scalability, programmability, nonlinear computation, training, and system integration. By positioning Fourier optics as a foundational branch within the broader landscape of optical neural computing, this review highlights the convergence of free-space, integrated, programmable, and hybrid photonic technologies toward next-generation artificial-intelligence hardware.

items.title: Optimization of Deep Learning Approach Using Chaotic Algorithm for Hepatitis Detection
items.abstract: Hepatitis still remains one of the major health issues in the world and is responsible for a significant amount of morbidity and mortality due to diseases related to the liver. Traditional approaches for hepatitis detection are costly, laboratorial, time-consuming, and error-prone. While AI and DL have enhanced medical diagnosis significantly, current models are prone to problems such as overfitting, long convergence period, and lack of generalization, which are primarily associated with inefficiency of hyperparameter optimization. In this research, the authors propose the use of optimized deep learning model based on Chaotic Optimization Algorithm (COA) for hepatitis detection. This approach combines Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) models with the application of COA, which allows optimizing such parameters as learning rate, hidden neurons, momentum, and weights initialization. Two publicly available datasets (the Kaggle Hepatitis Dataset and the UCI Hepatitis Dataset) have been used in this research. Data preprocessing steps including handling missing values, encoding, normalization, and splitting data into train and test datasets were applied. The COA-DNN gave results of 85.11% for accuracy, 77.83% for precision, 83.24% for recall, 79.85% for F1 score, and 0.9054 for AUC on the Kaggle dataset compared to the conventional DNN which had an accuracy of 57.45%. For the UCI dataset, the highest accuracy rate was achieved by COA-DNN at 96.76%, precision of 95.86%, recall of 88.82%, F1 score of 91.94%, and AUC of 0.9793. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Chaotic Optimization Algorithm; Deep Learning; Hepatitis Detection; Hyperparameter Optimization; Multi-Layer Perceptron; Neural.

items.title: Optimizing Agentic Artificial Intelligence to Improve Business Process Automation Efficiency through Modern Digital Technology
items.abstract: In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation (BPA) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision-making tasks. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule-based automation by enabling adaptive problem-solving, real-time context awareness, and cross-system collaboration. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes. Because this is a literature-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains.

items.title: Outcome-Anchored Credit Reallocation for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering
items.abstract: Agentic knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) requires large language models (LLMs) to solve complex questions through multi-turn interactions with a knowledge graph (KG). Outcome-supervised reinforcement learning derives verifiable outcome rewards from final answers but uniformly assigns each rollout's outcome-level advantage to all policy-generated tokens, creating a trajectory-to-operation mismatch since KG operations within a rollout can have varying effects on the search process and final answer. To address this, we propose Outcome-Anchored Credit Reallocation (OACR), which employs a training-only KG-state outcome model to estimate outcome-reward changes between adjacent KG search states and converts them into operation credit, from which token-wise weights are derived. These multiplicative weights reallocate token-level update magnitudes while preserving the sign of the outcome-level advantage at every generated token. Across three benchmarks, OACR achieves stronger overall performance than existing KGQA methods while using fewer inference-time LLM calls and tokens.

items.title: PERSISTENT HOMOLOGY ON LOCAL EXPLANATION SPACES: A TOPOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR EXPLAINABLE AI IN DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS
items.abstract: We propose a novel framework that re-architects explainable artificial intelligence within decision support systems by integrating persistent homology into the explanation pipeline. Conventional approaches treat local feature attributions, such as SHAP values, as isolated scalar values for individual predictions, thereby overlooking the multi-scale interaction structures that emerge across a dataset. To address this limitation, we embed a collection of local explanation vectors into a metric space and compute persistent homology using the Vietoris-Rips complex. This topological analysis yields a set of persistence diagrams that capture the birth and death of homology generators across multiple scales. From these diagrams, we construct a global interaction tensor that encodes the total persistence of topological features involving pairs of input features. This tensor is then incorporated into the decision support system’s utility model as a regularization term, which penalizes or rewards the co-occurrence of high-magnitude attributions on features that persistently interact across the dataset. The resulting system provides decision-makers with queryable, multi-scale explanations at selectable persistence thresholds, transforming the interface from a static explainer into a dynamic topological reasoning tool. For instance, a user can request all feature pairs with persistence above a given threshold in a specific homology dimension, and the system highlights those interactions in the explanation. The proposed method is realized using the Ripser algorithm for efficient computation on datasets of up to one hundred thousand instances, with periodic updates via a streaming variant. Our contribution is a principled mathematical framework that bridges topological data analysis and explainable AI, offering a new perspective on feature interaction discovery and explanation stability. The significance lies in its ability to reveal robust, higher-order interaction structures that are invisible to standard attribution methods, thereby enhancing the interpretability and trustworthiness of model-driven decisions.

items.title: Physics-informed deep learning for few-shot damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites under thermal variations
items.abstract: Guided wave (GW)-based damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites is fundamentally challenged by thermal variations and sparse sensor configurations, which induce severe baseline distortions and imaging artifacts. Traditional physical algorithms suffer from geometric ambiguity, while purely data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) models are hindered by opaque interpretability and prohibitive data dependency. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework, an artificial-intelligence-driven approach, for few-shot damage localization under thermal variations. The network is architected with a dual-stream input design, comprising a data-driven layer enhanced by a one-dimensional coordinate attention (1D-CA) mechanism and a physics-informed layer built upon a differentiable time-of-flight (TOF) physical imaging layer. A hybrid physics-constrained loss function is formulated to suppress non-physical artifacts and enforce physical consistency. GW signals are experimentally collected from manufactured CFRP composite plates, and a comparative investigation is performed to thoroughly assess the PIDL performance. Results indicate that:(1) The presence of physical penalties effectively mitigates artifacts and achieves robust localization across thermal gradients; (2) The model demonstrates superior spatial generalization that the integration of acoustic physical constraints acts as a crucial regularization mechanism, maintaining a highly accurate mean relative error (MRE) of 3.88% on completely unseen damage coordinates; (3) By implementing a few-shot transfer learning strategy, the PIDL model shows adaptability for dynamic operational environments (45 degrees Celsius (°C)-75 degrees Celsius (°C)). This work offers a physically interpretable and data-efficient paradigm for structural health monitoring (SHM) in dynamic operational environments.

items.title: Pilot study of a ChatGPT ‐based educational and counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Real-world implementation of large language models such as ChatGPT to enhance patient education remains limited. We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability and attitudes towards a ChatGPT-based counselling tool among patients and healthcare workers (HCWs) in a specialist infectious diseases clinic. METHODS: We conducted a prospective clinical implementation study in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic in Singapore from Jan 2025 to December 2025. Patients interacted with a custom ChatGPT-based chatbot prior to routine counselling by physicians or pharmacists. Responses were reviewed with patients subsequently during consultation. Post-interaction, patients and HCWs completed structured surveys incorporating domains from a validated survey tool: perceived risk, anxiety, technology/social influence and intention for future use. RESULTS: The chatbot was most frequently used for counselling on antiretroviral therapy initiation or switching, and sexual health advice. A total of 35 patients and 35 HCW assessments were analysed. Patients had greater perceived risk with the use of the chatbot compared to HCWs, as indicated by lower median scores (13, IQR 10-16; vs. 18, IQR 15-21), while anxiety scores were similar. Technology/social influence scores were high across both groups (overall median 20, IQR 19-22). Most participants indicated willingness for future use. Qualitative feedback highlighted improved patient understanding and more focused consultations, but concerns included lack of contextual nuance and occasional inaccuracies. CONCLUSIONS: The pilot implementation of a ChatGPT-based counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic was feasible and generally acceptable to patients and HCWs. Further studies are required to evaluate accuracy and clinical effectiveness before broader implementation.
